very nice place for a little sleep with an RV more than 20 locations, without service.

très jolie place pour un petit dodo avec un VR plus de 20 emplacements, sans service.

quebec-informal.name: casse croute cartier
quebec-informal.notes: parking lot near the restaurant, beach front stayed there one night no problem, bathroom across the street

quebec-informal.name: Walmart - 2nd location in town, not the supercenter
quebec-informal.notes: Typical Walmart, but not a supercenter where parking can sometimes be restricted. Close to Hwy A40, but we found road noise pretty much died off by 10-11pm. Store closes at 9. Multiple RVs next to us and about 10 by morning. MacDonalds and Tim's across the street.

quebec-informal.name: Provincial Park Reserve (west Linwood)
quebec-informal.notes: It's a little driveway and a boat launch. Not leveled, few locations came (as if it was part of ther daily walk). A little noise from the far away hiway. sigh for no camping. But it's like having your private million dollars place.

quebec-informal.name: Stationnement du traversier
quebec-informal.notes: Grass field near the ferry. Seem to be owned by the ferry company. Good for small rig. Arrived late with the ferry. It seems to be a parking. Passed the night without being disturbed

quebec-informal.name: Parking Centre Sportif Alexis Berube
quebec-informal.notes: Nice quiet parking in a front of Centre Sportif. Library very near. Shops, gas station, coffee some 2 minutes by car.

quebec-informal.name: Pappy's BBQ joint
quebec-informal.notes:
Great BBQ joint with craft beer and extensive bbq menu.
Hans the owner opens up a super grassy spot for boondockers as long as you buy his succulent food. I feel that's a fair deal and it's real tasty, cheaper than a campsite, no cooking and no dishes
As bonus the sunset is awesome. See pictures.
Highly recommended and there are some GF and vegetarian options.

quebec-informal.name: BEECHWOOD COMMUNITY PARK
quebec-informal.notes:
Nice park with picnic tables.
Small boat ramp.
Big rig can park & turn. 
Toilets
Gate closes at 10:00pm
No overnight

quebec-informal.name: Parc riverain de la Boyer
quebec-informal.notes:
Small parking lot accessible for motorhomes or trailers 25 feet or less. Sleeping stop possible if you are 100% autonomous and very discreet (nothing outside your vehicle) Trails, tables and shelters. Please leave the place cleaner when you leave than when you arrive.

Petit stationnement accessible pour un motorisés ou une caravanes portés de 25 pieds ou moins. Arrêt dodo possible si vous êtes 100% autonome et très discret ( rien a l’extérieur de votre véhicule) Sentiers, tables et abris. Svp laisser l’endroit plus propre a votre départ qu’à votre arrivée.

quebec-informal.name: Atlantic Superstore
quebec-informal.notes:
In the parking lot just in front of the store they have nice space

We ask to the Service counter and it was OK

Nice place just after or before the ferry

quebec-informal.name: Sentier Missisquoi Trail head parking
quebec-informal.notes:
Small parking
Like a pull out on a country road 300 meters away from trail

quebec-informal.name: Pigeon Hill
quebec-informal.notes: Great spot ocean one side fishing port the other side, long ocean side beach.

quebec-informal.name: parking lot at the gate
quebec-informal.notes: we arrived after 16H00 and the day use is good until 20H00. so we could pay for a camp site,  but when we asked if can sleep in the parking lot the Ranger almost laughed and said yes, and actually it is the best site because it has WiFi, toilet(in the building) and picnic tables on the grass. the only thing is no fire. so we slept here and will do some hiking today, and probably will sleep here again tonight.

quebec-informal.name: Great lunch stop with kids
quebec-informal.notes: This is a 6$ per child  small amusement park with 4 inflatable games, parking lot big and you can stop and rest while kids play, if you are in or outbound of Montreal

quebec-informal.name: Pulperie de Chicoutimi
quebec-informal.notes: Parking for bus, caravan and rv the day but you can stay here at night.  No services but clean and secured.

quebec-informal.name: halte routière du bic
quebec-informal.notes: petit parking, pas de pancarte interdiction de dormir mais restriction de 4h maximum, jy suis reste 6h45 et sans problème, aucun son, toilette accessible, gens respectueux

quebec-informal.name: Canada
quebec-informal.notes: Municipal parking close to river st maurice with gig toilet 24 hrs parc free

quebec-informal.name: Rue de le eglise
quebec-informal.notes: Small car park next to the church. Free to stay the night. Small donation box. No facilities (toilets etc) however a beautiful morning view of the st Lawrence river. Very peaceful and safe location.

quebec-informal.name: St-Hugues
quebec-informal.notes: Deux stationnements pour Rv aménagé et identifié.  Stationnement en asphalte et en plein soleil.  Près d'une école et d'un parc a chien.  Des règles sont affichée. La nuit a été  tranquille.

quebec-informal.name: Source du rang 15
quebec-informal.notes: Petite halte très chouette au bord du rang avec toilette sèche, tables, foyer, source...

quebec-informal.name: Parking behind the library
quebec-informal.notes: parking avec permission du centre d'information touristique de passer la nuit derrière l'église et la bibliothèque, sans service. Nous étions seul, donc très calme.

quebec-wild.name: Cape Blow Me Down Trail - South Shore Outer Bay
quebec-wild.notes: Beautiful place to sleep at the parking lot to a hiking trail on a 650m high mountain. SUPER view from the mountain, highly recommended!

quebec-wild.name: Cabot Trail - OK
quebec-wild.notes: Near river. Has picnic area 3.5km from here

quebec-wild.name: Cabot Trail - Pleasent Bay - TOP
quebec-wild.notes: Watch Hammer roost directly cliff beautiful secluded, great for whales, totally quiet. Perfect for small van or tent

quebec-wild.name: CabotTrail - Pleasent Bay - TOP
quebec-wild.notes:
Hammer sleeping place right on the cliff! Wonderful whale watching!
No service

quebec-wild.name: Mi'kmawey Debert Interpretative Trail head
quebec-wild.notes: Beautiful place to sleep and picnic area. Unfortunately, close to road. Start to nem beautiful short trail.

quebec-wild.name: Gaspe West - OK
quebec-wild.notes: Roost on knoll beside main road. Visible exposed by road, mediocre traffic, the wind. OK to stay but was already better places!

quebec-wild.name: Gaspe West - TOP
quebec-wild.notes: Very nice place to sleep right on a lake. Unfortunately on road but little traffic.

quebec-wild.name: Gaspé - Nördlich Forillon Park - NAJA
quebec-wild.notes: Sleeping next to road on Hill. Legal lot of traffic, cars look a if they look good and exposed to the wind. Was more a night shelter because everything was very inhabited.

quebec-wild.name: Gaspé - Richtung Süden nach Tadussac - NICE
quebec-wild.notes: Very nice place to sleep right on the lake. There were canoeing and stayed. During the day, loud trucks, at night it was quiet. For a very nice location. 4x4 Strecker goes into the bushes, where it might be quiet, but I have not abgecheckt!

quebec-wild.name: Level-sur-Quévillon - NICE
quebec-wild.notes:
Cute sleeping place right on the river. Has some black flies and near road, but hardly any traffic. Beautiful sunset, relaxing water rapids sounds makes you feel alone..
Phone service not so good, but ok.

quebec-wild.name: Nord-West Roberval auf 167 - OK
quebec-wild.notes: Cute sleeping place right on the lake. Had evening many mosquitoes and road nearby, but was still quiet at night as there is little traffic.

quebec-wild.name: Woody Point - OK
quebec-wild.notes: Directly behind water reservoir well hidden place to sleep and also the starting point for BigLookOut Trail

quebec-wild.name: Rue de la Block, Tracadie-Sheila
quebec-wild.notes: Small spot at the end of the road. Restrooms at the Visitor Center (500m).

quebec-wild.name: Forest camping near Hwy 299
quebec-wild.notes: Wild camping at a snow free forest road. Very quiet at night.

quebec-wild.name: Parc National des Grands Jardins
quebec-wild.notes: Gravel area next to the highway, not much traffic at night, no facilities

quebec-wild.name: Stone Beach
quebec-wild.notes:
Fantastic place right by the sea. 4x4 needed to come here in the snow, otherwise it would be OK. On the way to the square you can find other good spots. Be sure to take Chem du Phare as the other route is very washed out. 
......
Traumhafter Platz direkt am Meer. 4x4 brauchten wir um hier bei Schnee hin zu kommen sonst müsste es gehen. Auf dem Weg zu dem Platz findet man noch andere Top Spots.

quebec-wild.name: Chertsey
quebec-wild.notes: For Stay one night is ok. It is a Hikingparking near the scool. Nice and quite.

quebec-wild.name: La Baie (Saguenay)
quebec-wild.notes:
RV parking in front of boat cruise terminal. Free. Wifi

Parking R. V. Pres du pavillon des croisieristes. Gratuit. WIFI

quebec-wild.name: P2 Sentier Des Appalaches/ Appalachian Trail Parking
quebec-wild.notes: Overnight parking only - nothing else. Appalachian Trail

quebec-wild.name: P1-Sentier National - National Trials
quebec-wild.notes: National trails parking with no amenities

quebec-wild.name: Quebec Cycle-way
quebec-wild.notes:
200 m to the west of the marina. 5 km from the Citadel. Angle cote Gilmour and bd Champlin. Picnic area, tables, drinking water fountain. Noise from the road. 

A 200 m a l'ouest de la marina. 5 km de la Citadelle. Angle cote Gilmour et bd Champlin. Aire de pique nique, tables, fontaine a eau potable. Bruit de la route.

quebec-wild.name: Pointe Sapin
quebec-wild.notes:
Parking near the port and the beach. Wireless. 

Parking pres du port et de la plage. Wifi.

quebec-wild.name: Pins river
quebec-wild.notes:
Just of rt 500 between Happy Valley and Churchill Falls a nice spot right on a fast streaming river.
many mosquitos and flies. several fire pits and a memorial in the bush.

quebec-wild.name: Baie Comeau Q.
quebec-wild.notes:
gravel parking on the coast, several spots right on the beach, a waterfall and plenty berries to harvest along the road.
Just north of Baie Comeau Q. off the 138. A boat launch and gazebo on the edge of the St Lawrence river

quebec-wild.name: Iles De La Madeleine - Ile Du Cap Aux Meules.
quebec-wild.notes:
Parking area, in the middle of the dunes, Near the beach, at the head of the hospital. 

Aire de stationnement, au milieu des dunes, Pres de la plage, au cap de l'hopital.

quebec-wild.name: Iles De La Madeleine. Cap Aux Meules
quebec-wild.notes:
Parking in front of Eastern Kings Sportsplex Arena. Opposite the rue du port, departure from the ferry. 

Stationnement devant Eastern Kings Sportsplex Arena. En face la rue du port, depart du ferry.

quebec-wild.name: Near Caraquet
quebec-wild.notes: On the road 145 to a cap with sandy road right above the beach, many places there to stay. Sea not really fitting for swimming.

quebec-wild.name: French Village Beach
quebec-wild.notes: Parkinglot in front of the dunes, nice sandy beach.

quebec-wild.name: On Dirtroad To Cape North
quebec-wild.notes: Big area next to the road with great view above St. Lawrence Bay. Road in not so good condition, big holes, may be muddy/slippery when raining. If you walk up the hill a little further you can get cell service.

quebec-wild.name: Baddek
quebec-wild.notes:
Parking near a church, above the harbor. Wireless. 

Parking pres d'une eglise, au-dessus du port. Wifi.

quebec-wild.name: Cap Egmont Lighthouse
quebec-wild.notes: Small dirt road to the lighthouse. Place is directly on the south coast. View of New Brunswick. (We had a stormy night...)

quebec-wild.name: Meat Cove Ridge
quebec-wild.notes:
On the side of the dirt road. Not for too large vehicule. Whale watching.

Sur le côté de la piste. Pour les véhicules pas trop larges. Observation d'une baleine.

quebec-wild.name: Cap d'Or
quebec-wild.notes:
Parking at the Cap d'Or lighthouse, Very quiet.
....
Parking du phare Cap D'Or. Très tranquille.

quebec-wild.name: Ingonish Harbour
quebec-wild.notes:
Parking at the wharf. 
.....
Stationnement au bord du quai.

quebec-wild.name: Port Aux Basques
quebec-wild.notes:
Parking Marine Atlantic. Above the harbor. 

Parking Marine Atlantique. Au-dessus du port.

quebec-wild.name: Three Mile Rock
quebec-wild.notes:
Picnic area by the sea. Superb panorama. 

Aire de pique-nique au de la mer. Superbe panorama.

quebec-wild.name: Jemseg Ferry Rd NICE
quebec-wild.notes:
Secluded Road right at the St. Johns river. Not far from Gagetown ferry. The Ferry is not there anymore (June 2017)...

Not suitable for trailers...

quebec-wild.name: Vieux Fort
quebec-wild.notes:
Plateau above the city, Near the cemetery. Spectacular view. 

Plateau au-dessus de la ville, Pres du cimetiere. Vue spectaculaire.

quebec-wild.name: Halte routière - Les Petites Sept Iles
quebec-wild.notes:
A seaside rest area in the company of gray seals that howl like wolves. Superb beach. 

Une aire de repos en bord de mer en compagnie de phoques gris qui hurlent comme des loups. Superbe plage.

quebec-wild.name: Rivière Natashquan
quebec-wild.notes:
At the edge of the river Natashquan along the track and the bridge built in 2013 before Kegaska, very quiet. 


Au bord de la rivière Natashquan en bord de piste et du pont construit en 2013 avant Kegaska, très tranquille.

quebec-wild.name: Big Pond
quebec-wild.notes:
Flat ground, gravel, roadside


Terrain plat, gravillonne, en bord de route

quebec-wild.name: At Highway 50
quebec-wild.notes: it is a gravel place near Highway, like a small rest area with a picnic table and garbage bin, good for a night

quebec-wild.name: Pointe-Yamachiche
quebec-wild.notes: parking place from the bird watching point , no sign for no overnight, the trail to the point is allowed with dogs and 1,5 km long , also a boardwalk with two great views in the biosphere reservation

quebec-wild.name: McGraw Brook
quebec-wild.notes:
Very nice site at the river, beautiful view, we stopped here just for a picnic.
.....
Moderator Note: More recent Users stayed overnight with success.

quebec-wild.name: Dorchester Picnic place
quebec-wild.notes: nice picnic area with tables, shelter and fire rings, no sign for no overnight

quebec-wild.name: Near Walton
quebec-wild.notes: There’s 4-7 campsites around here - may require some serious 4x4 because the puddles are deep. But they’re all private and have campfires. Amazing views of the bay. I think you can follow a path down to the ocean. Looks like it was an old bridge / road.

quebec-wild.name: Lark Harbour - bay of islands
quebec-wild.notes: Sleeping place at the end of the fishing docks in Lark harbour. Beaufiful sunset.

quebec-wild.name: Carrière - bivouac sentier Mont Uapishka
quebec-wild.notes: This quarry serves as a camping site for hikers who leave on the summits of the Uapishka Mountains.

quebec-wild.name: Labrador City - Ski area parking
quebec-wild.notes:
Smoky Mountain, at the ski lift, quiet.

Smoky Mountain, Ski Lift,  ruhig.

quebec-wild.name: Happy Valley - Goose Bay
quebec-wild.notes: Parkplatz am See. Sehr ruhig. Blick über den See.

quebec-wild.name: Trans Labrador Highway 510
quebec-wild.notes: Road Maintenance area, turn left northbound. Lot of open space.

quebec-wild.name: Grouse lake & Teapot lake
quebec-wild.notes: Small treed site off of logging road at Grouse lake. Gravel parking lot with boat launch at Teapot lake.

quebec-wild.name: Rouyn-Noranda
quebec-wild.notes:
Behind the end of paved road in a small forest, dirty gravel parking, quiet.
Good for one night. Not far away from Walmart.

quebec-wild.name: Rivière Péribonka
quebec-wild.notes:
Nice campspot at the river Péribonka, it's like a fjord of Lake Saint-Jean.
The access is a small dirt road, not for big campers. Great view over the river.
It's really a beautiful spot.

quebec-wild.name: Pointe de pruches
quebec-wild.notes:
Near the beach. No "camping not allowed" signs.
--
Près de la plage. Pas de panneaux d'interdiction de dormir

quebec-wild.name: Alma Trails - 4x4 access
quebec-wild.notes: Follow the 4x4 trails behind Alma to a small flat clearing at the side of the trail.  Trail is large round rocks in places, drive slow. 4X4 with good tires, clearance and low range strongly recommended.  Some low hanging trees over the trail.

quebec-wild.name: forest shelter near river
quebec-wild.notes: just off the highway, a few km up a gravel road, lies this gem of a wild camping spot, in the middle of the forest. there is an outhouse on site.  hike 200m to the river for swimming (with lots of mosquitoes).  This is mostly for vans, class Bs, or very small tow behind campers.

quebec-wild.name: Patc de l’Ile aux foin
quebec-wild.notes:
Ile aux Foins public park. Picnic tables, pit toilets.
.....
Parc de l'Ile aux Foins public park parking picknik tables pit toilets

quebec-wild.name: The Arches Provincial Park
quebec-wild.notes: We stayed in the parking lot overnight with a spectacular view of the ocean. There are no signs to disallow overnight parking. Very quiet with only the sound of the surf.

quebec-wild.name: Mutton Cove Beach
quebec-wild.notes: Superb spot by the beach. Too perfect for words. We just spent a whole day and night. Quiet, private, paved way up to the beach, so no 4x4 needed. Just be mindful of the tidal variation and do not lit up any fire before 19:00. No infrastructure, just the most beautiful scenery. Enjoy.

quebec-wild.name: Cartwright Access Road Quarry
quebec-wild.notes: Good place off the road for overnight stop. Many bugs - like everywhere else in the interior.

quebec-wild.name: Happy Valley-Goose Bay, Labrador.
quebec-wild.notes: Small spot at the end of a very sandy track. The road to here is littered with garbage but the spot itself is clean. Weather station blocks a bit of the view but still very nice sunrise over water in the morning. 4x4 might be required depending on surface conditions. Room to house a tent or a small trailer but not much more.

quebec-wild.name: Rest area near Cabot trail
quebec-wild.notes: Rest area in the forest (gravel road to reach the site) very quiet with tables. You are in the middle of nowhere, it's a perfect site.

quebec-wild.name: Beautiful Place close to Economy Falls
quebec-wild.notes: Sideroad with amazing view over the bay and sun until late. Close to hiking trail to economy falls. NO Mosquitoes or flies!!! Just perfect.

quebec-wild.name: Pleasant View Beach
quebec-wild.notes:
End of road leading to Sea shore.
Beautiful beach 
Not for large rigs as impossible to turn around.
Small trailers and tents can even camp on the beach.

quebec-wild.name: Point North, Trans-Tiaga West
quebec-wild.notes: Old road and clearing on hill. Nice level site and quiet. Tried to camp at the point but too crowded

quebec-wild.name: Pont Ferme. End of the Road
quebec-wild.notes: End of a long gravel road next to a stream. Fairly rough with an unsafe bridge at the end so doubt much traffic. Very quiet

quebec-wild.name: Towerview
quebec-wild.notes: 2 flat spots at the end of 4wd road on hill. Next to radio tower

quebec-wild.name: Ghost Town Joutel
quebec-wild.notes: Former site of the mining town Joutel. lots of roads but no houses. take your choice.

quebec-wild.name: England's Lake
quebec-wild.notes: Lake side camping on the embankment dam just off the service road.  Take Middletown Road off the 344 Highway at Melford (south of Mulgrave).  It's a short drive on a well maintained service road to the dam.

quebec-wild.name: Catalone Gut
quebec-wild.notes:
Open gravel space at the water. 

Not very leveled but ok.

quebec-wild.name: Jamieson Road
quebec-wild.notes:
Space at the end of the street. Directly behind the shoreline. 

Not very leveled but doable. 

If you have high clearance/an offroad vehicle you can go direct on to the gravel beach.

quebec-wild.name: Dans la nature
quebec-wild.notes:
The area is been used by fishermen and workers. 
I took the dirt road and at the 1st intersection with a private road there is a small area where you can park in the forest just before the private road. The neighbors were okay to let us stay. Tent okay. 4WD recommended.

quebec-wild.name: New Harbour Beach
quebec-wild.notes:
Nice place near the beach with fire pit. Not far from the highway but no traffic.
Not for big rigs.

quebec-wild.name: Crown land site
quebec-wild.notes:
There is some spot at this location. This is crown land close to the park Algonquin. You will need a high clearance vehicle to access the trail.

Roughly enough space for a JKU to pass between the trees, trailers needed some magic.

Be careful in the hunting season!

quebec-wild.name: Minnow lake - Crown Land
quebec-wild.notes:
Crow Land camping spot on side of a Small lake stock with lake trout.
Must have 4x4 vehicle

quebec-wild.name: Goose Creek - Crown Land
quebec-wild.notes:
Located in the Bay of Fundy just our side the national park territory this is one of my most memorable campsites. Once you leave the main road it's about 28km of rough gravel roads and a steep long descent for the last 7km. ( expect 1h of travel once you leave the main road )

4x4 / offroad vehicle is a MUST

quebec-wild.name: Chéticamp - Cell Tower
quebec-wild.notes: This is on top of the mountain. along steep drive but with a very nice view of the region. There is a private spot near the tower or other trails

quebec-wild.name: Shiner Lake - Crown Land
quebec-wild.notes: Shiner Lake is a Crown Land camping spot with multiple fire pits or sites available. Very easy access for any vehicle.

quebec-wild.name: K&P Trail - Crown Land
quebec-wild.notes:
There is a few places along this trail which goes from Kingston to Pembrook were you could set up for the night. It's recommended checking on the Crown Land website to be sure you're not set up on the privet land section that this trail crosses.  It's a very nice drive :)

Ontario Cround Land Map
http://www.gisapplication.lrc.gov.on.ca/CLUPA/Index.html?site=CLUPA&viewer=CLUPA&locale=en-US

K&P info
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%26P_Rail_Trail

quebec-wild.name: Timber Lake
quebec-wild.notes: Ther are 2 very nice Crown Land ( wild camping ) spots each with access to the lake. They are close to the road and easy access. There is another spot a few hundred meters east which is not as nice but has a boat launch.

quebec-wild.name: Greater Madawaska
quebec-wild.notes: This is a very cute discrete camp spot just off a gravel road trail. We have stopped twice at this campsite and have loved it every time :)

quebec-wild.name: Calabogie Power Line
quebec-wild.notes: This is a nice off-roading trail with a few challenges nice spots to stop for the night. 4x4 with a minimum of 10" clearance is recommended.

quebec-wild.name: Wabun Lake
quebec-wild.notes: There is a sign posted no camping right before you get to the boat launch. HOWEVER, there are several campsites on the road leading to the boat launch, before the no camping sign, and there aren't any other signs that I could see. A kind person gave us their campsite as they were leaving and said that he got fined for camping near the boat launch last year, but that you were fine so long as you didn't camp anywhere after the NO CAMPING sign.

quebec-wild.name: Griffith
quebec-wild.notes: This location has a few spots to set-up and has water access not too far away. This is a great cute option for a night or two.

quebec-wild.name: Crown Land
quebec-wild.notes: There are 2 very nice clearings, each with a nice fire pit on this trail. A great large isolated place to rest up. Don't go further than the one I have marked on the map the trail after that one gets tighter and unpassable by vehicle fast. Nice trails to take a hike nearby.

quebec-wild.name: K & P - Boat Launch
quebec-wild.notes:
This is a small unofficial boat launch on the side of the K& P trail. It has a great view and place to park 2 to 3 vehicles. Its very exposed but if there is a nice sky worth stopping for a night. 

I personally would not stay longer than a kick overnight because it's not during the day there normally is a lot of action on that section of the rail and would not be quiet.

quebec-wild.name: Cape Spencer Lookout
quebec-wild.notes:
Great ocean view looking out over a cliff. Site is large enough and grassy flat to accommodate camping and is accessible by stock 4x4 but recommend a vehicle modified for off-road.
*No Way with a stock 4x4*
*Not recommended for an Overlander Vehicle*

quebec-wild.name: Parc des Écluses
quebec-wild.notes:
Huge area with lots of wild camping options, right by the river on graveled parking or under big trees on grass (we stayed in the shade of the trees, the grass was dry). You see big ships passing the locks.
Sign says 'no swimming/diving/boating'.

quebec-wild.name: Le Clocher
quebec-wild.notes: You can park in the parking lot.  There is a service for white water rafting.  The old church has a resto, climbing wall, library, WiFi, and more.  Go to lac Eden, there is a public beach and camping is possible as there is no bylaw.

quebec-wild.name: Little Lake
quebec-wild.notes:
Level parking pad right next to a small lake just off the highway. Small campers only. Visible from highway.

Not sure how things look during summer (high season), but there are currently no signs prohibiting camping. Free.

quebec-wild.name: chemin aéroport
quebec-wild.notes: Nice place and quite good for stop in the area

quebec-wild.name: Old Bridge
quebec-wild.notes:
I think, here was an old bridge for the highway 1. So you have here two roads, that ends on the river were you can stay. The road to South is asphalt, the road to north is gravel. 
be careful with big vehicle- both roads are dead end roads, so you can't turn around with big vehicles. 
The place is a bit noisy because it is 15m away from the highway. But it is behind the bushes, so nobody can see you an distrub you.

quebec-wild.name: Deer Lake Boat Launch
quebec-wild.notes:
Great gravel parking lot with no amenities. 

Signs say no camping within 66ft of water and no camping (*not overnight parking)

Moose, frogs and mosquitoes!

Leave space for boat trailers to turn around!!!!

quebec-wild.name: Wilson point
quebec-wild.notes: It's a dead end near the sea with a pic nic table no amenities though

quebec-wild.name: Warf alley
quebec-wild.notes: It his kind a hard to see but a soons as you get of the bridge thats goes to misou take the first small road on you're right It's going to bring you almost under the bridge

quebec-wild.name: Casey airstrip
quebec-wild.notes: Good place abandonned a long time ago. to sleep far from everything, you can go on the river or the airstrip.

quebec-wild.name: La pointe
quebec-wild.notes: Petit spot de campement rustique sur les terre de la couronne

quebec-wild.name: 19k / West of Lourdes de Blanc Sablon
quebec-wild.notes: Open, flat, hard surfaced area overlooking the water. Only 200m off the road but very quiet.

quebec-wild.name: Parc de la source
quebec-wild.notes:
Quiet place for one night
Not Many choice in this area

quebec-wild.name: Halte pont rouge
quebec-wild.notes: Picnic area where we slept one night. Quiet despite the road nearby. Beautiful view of the red wooden bridge

quebec-wild.name: halte routière
quebec-wild.notes:
Very large parking lot, ideal to sleep
--
très grand parking idéal pour arrêt dodo

quebec-wild.name: Port au Choix
quebec-wild.notes: Not sure what this is but it is a dirt road leading to a parking area. A little noise from the road but quiet at night. Great view of the ocean.

quebec-wild.name: Reverse rapids New Brunswick, Canada
quebec-wild.notes: Quiet carpark on south side of bridge. Away from the noise of the paper mill. Not quite so scenic but a lot quieter

quebec-wild.name: Roadside pull off
quebec-wild.notes: Large spot next to a not so busy road. Close to the old nipissing road, good spot for lunch or an overnight stop.

quebec-wild.name: Oceanside
quebec-wild.notes:
To be reached by a long gravel road with partly bad conditions, but reachable with a 4x2 nevertheless. Spot directly at the ocean surrounded by small cliffs, caves and a little river. perfect place for a campfire. 
maybe some locals show up on weekends

quebec-wild.name: Meat Cove Beach
quebec-wild.notes:
Campspot is ok. Right below the official campsite directly at the beach. Some locals went by, but no problems with overnight camping. Might be different when the official campsite is open. Steep gravel road.
Camp site was open and booked solid, the attendant suggested we use this public beach. lane down is a little tough, some 2wd folks were struggling to get up.

quebec-wild.name: At Pinus River
quebec-wild.notes: On the road from Happy Valley to Churchill Falls. Near to the road. Too narrow for big rigs.

quebec-wild.name: popular sand spit camp
quebec-wild.notes: popular wild camp on a sand spit with many caravans in high season. Long beach, drift wood and plenty of generators and ATVs. Location is great, view of St.Lawrence gulf, Anticosti and inlet. Sandy but every RV can get there. A even nicer camp is west from the  outlet of the river where you do not have to camp in the sand, there you are on elevated ground.

quebec-wild.name: shipwreck point
quebec-wild.notes: Tiny spot right at the sea. Short hike to a shipwreck and picnic tables. Fantastic coastal scenery. Access via a very narrow dirt track. Wind protected tent camping possible in nearby quarry, but only accessible on foot. Unfortunately there is a rotting whale nearby, very bad smells in 2018.

quebec-wild.name: White sand beach 4x4 camp
quebec-wild.notes: Quiet bay, clean beach, white sand. Canooing possible in cristal clear bay. Nearby uninteresting old mining ruins. Access on very narrow dirt track, high  clearance recommended, 4x4 in wet conditions.

quebec-wild.name: Grafton Island
quebec-wild.notes: Small space privileged view on the River, perfect lot for a stop to eat, sleep or swim in the River. Lowering is right next to a sign of speed 60

quebec-wild.name: Crooked Creek NB
quebec-wild.notes: 1 of a couple wild camping spots along Crooked Creek river. when you come to a Y in the road. if you go to the right it will take you to a look off area. left to river for camping.) there is a spot for a tent. recommended 4wd. great for RTT, overlanding vehicle or overlander trailer

quebec-wild.name: Churchill River
quebec-wild.notes: At the trailhead to the Churchill Falls. Near to the bridge across the Churchill River.

quebec-wild.name: Miron River
quebec-wild.notes: Between Churchill Falls and Labrador City. Near to Miron River.

quebec-wild.name: On the road to manic 3
quebec-wild.notes: A good place for one night between Fermont and Baie-Comeau. At the 389/manic3 junction.

quebec-wild.name: franquelin

beautiful view of the river with picnic tables, quiet to sleep.

belle vue sur le fleuve avec tables picnic, tranquille pour dormir.

quebec-wild.name: Rocky beach down woods road

quebec-wild.name: Grosses Roches down by the boat ramp
quebec-wild.notes: Public boat launch with small parking area.    Steep road to and from off the Main Street, with gravel right at the top that may create traction issues for some vehicles.

quebec-wild.name: Parking
quebec-wild.notes:
Large free parking near paid parking. Quiet night.

Grand parking gratuit près des parkings payants. Nuit calme.

quebec-wild.name: 1001 nice campsites
quebec-wild.notes: Vast plateau with boundless wild camping spots. Stay as far away from the little travelled main road as you wish, enjoy the view on the wild, lake doted scenery. Can be windy up here, but quietness guaranteed!

small parking for RV max 21 feet with picnic table

Can sleep 3 night near the church very beautiful place

peux dormir 3 nuits (vérifier avec les propriétaires du motel).

quebec-wild.name: Metro grocery store
quebec-wild.notes: located between car dealership and residential area, slight inclination to the parking lot, a few light post on parking.

quebec-wild.name: Arena, sport center
quebec-wild.notes: parking lot across arena, slight a for to parking, adjacent to school yard and river.

quebec-wild.name: Pabineau Falls
quebec-wild.notes: Incredible falls. Enough space for many RVs.  Calm and gorgeous.

quebec-wild.name: Livingstone shore road
quebec-wild.notes: Wild campsite at the end of the road. Close to farm so be discreet. Locals came to have a campfire by the beach on Saturday night. ATVs can pass by. Beautiful beach. Good for swimming too.

quebec-wild.name: Stationnement
quebec-wild.notes:
Parking near the harbor. A lot of people come and go until 22:00. Perfect if you are stuck for a night.

Stationnement près du port. Beaucoup de va et vien jusqu’à 22:00. Parfait si on est mal pris pour une nuit.

quebec-wild.name: ste sophie , laurentides quebec
quebec-wild.notes: new clean Parking space for 4 really big RV Relatively quiet in the St Sophie municipality still close to the road No any sign prohibiting overnight parking RV dump station with non potable water near the toilet at the entrance. Good cell reception

quebec-wild.name: mascouche..parc à chien
quebec-wild.notes:
Large parking lot ideal for the night and market path nearby

Google translated from original:
grand parking idéal pour la nuit et sentier de marché à proximite

quebec-wild.name: St-Narcisse (Rimouski)
quebec-wild.notes: Roadside, on the edge of a calm river. (Halte routière.) no cellphone reception

quebec-wild.name: Rosemont
quebec-wild.notes:
A few minutes away from Rosemont metro station. Free parking, with others trucks / RVs parked here. Rather quiet for a city place , not extremely nice (parking around) but well located next to Mile End and Petite Italie with lot of restaurants around. There is a small place for kids to play and bike road. 
A boulangerie and laverie not far.

quebec-wild.name: Trois Rivières
quebec-wild.notes:
The GPS location noted on the place is difficult to find. Go first to these place : 46.31184 -72.56947. Then pass under the bridge.

A nice place to spend a night near a river and at 3 km from Walmart. No sign of no parking. Some fishermen. Wind 

Make sure to drive behind the Hôtel les Suites de Laviolette all the way to the end, turn left at the stop sign, and keep going even with the construction site. There's a small gravel road which leads to the location.

quebec-wild.name: Grand Bay Park
quebec-wild.notes: Nice, quiet and level parking lot in a beautiful setting right next to a sandy beach and walking trails. Great camp spot when visiting this area. There are no restrictions to staying in this parking lot as is common in Newfoundland. Highly recommend to stay here.

quebec-wild.name: road 103
quebec-wild.notes: Spot at the riverside  between Fredericton and Edmunston. Along road 103. Ok for one night, table avaiable.

quebec-wild.name: Louse Creek Air Stip (Abandoned)
quebec-wild.notes: Crown Land, massive area on abandoned airstrip. Road in is fine, last bit is a bit of a slope but okay for my Class B.  Go down the far end for more privacy.

quebec-wild.name: Wreck Cove Hydro Reservoir
quebec-wild.notes:
Quiet place in the highlands of Cape Breton directly next to the road with direct view to the water (on the opposite side of the road). Bring bug repellent!

Access over a rough and sometimes steep gravel road (about 6-7 km from Cabot trail).

quebec-wild.name: Montagne du diable
quebec-wild.notes: up we go..by 4x4 with our trailler. hard road really need 4x4 but what a view once your up... on the way theire is some place where you can stop and camp too.

quebec-wild.name: Clear water lake
quebec-wild.notes: Beautiful spot by the water. You can camp there for quick night and use fire pit around you. Use the Little mud trail next to the lake to find the spot. There’s a sign ‘’ private ‘’ but no shack around and no sign of private propriety. Its probably Just a guy that dosent want the spot to be found...

quebec-wild.name: Kildare Seafood Product Wharf
quebec-wild.notes:
On Wharf Road just before the wharf there is a road to the right to a level spot overlooking the fisherman & boats. Small road crescent off a dirty road that surrounds a large rock that may be a monument and there is a small working automated lighthouse nearby. Grass and a fabulous view of the ocean (ok ok Golfe of St-Lawrence). This is near the most western portion of PEI. 

No cell signal for Rogers or Fido. But cell signal available for Telus

quebec-wild.name: Lac Mogridge
quebec-wild.notes: Nice place with a view on the lake, located along a short unpaved side road.  Some noise from passing vehicles on the 389, very quite at night.

quebec-wild.name: Gull lake
quebec-wild.notes: Lot of large camping spots along a wide unpaved side road.  Very quiet spot!

quebec-wild.name: Cox’s Cove Falls
quebec-wild.notes: Small parking lot with view at the falls, at the end of a 3 K gravel road. Really inviting to take a dip in the pool of the falls. The water is nice, clear and warm. Short hike to the top of the falls. Not for big RV’s, truckcampers are ok.

quebec-wild.name: Hidden Falls
quebec-wild.notes: Nice and very quiet parking lot between the Sea and the Hidden Falls. Oceanside, but be cautious about swimming with the tides.

quebec-wild.name: Port aux Port East
quebec-wild.notes: Along a short gravelroad at the stoney beach.

quebec-wild.name: Crabbes
quebec-wild.notes: Beautiful view and sunset above the ocean, park at the border of a cliff. Drive the short cemetery road and continue a little to find a grassroad.

quebec-wild.name: caraquet
quebec-wild.notes: Nice place To sleep when the commerce was close...large parking and quiet

quebec-wild.name: Stop on the 132
quebec-wild.notes: large parking with table et garbage close To the river and the road.

quebec-wild.name: Pic de l'aube
quebec-wild.notes:
Small parking lot at the beginning of the trail after 40 kilometers of gravel road.

Petit stationnement au début du sentier de randonnée après 40 kilometres de chemin de terre.

quebec-wild.name: McNulty Lake
quebec-wild.notes:
Great Off road camping spot for relaxing, swimming & Fishing. Once off the road it’s will only take you 20min to get to the lake. ( U most park on top of the hill, not a direct lake access, but very small walk )

Strongly recommend a 4x4. I did the trail with my stock Jeep JK with no problem you just need to go slow and pic your line properly. When I went all the obstacles were marked with Trail tape :)

quebec-wild.name: Road 17
quebec-wild.notes: Large gravel terrain aside the road, surrounded by low forest. It’s a pity that some people leave their used toilet paper after camping at this spot.

quebec-wild.name: Saint-Léonard Parish
quebec-wild.notes: Quiet camping spot with a nice view.  On a sand and grass area along a sandy farmers road.  Maybe not a good idea to use this spot at the moment of harvesting, could be used by farmers.

quebec-wild.name: Cabot Trail
quebec-wild.notes: A parking area fairly level for one large rig or 2 or 3 small rigs. Ocean view. Access to beach is possible but not easy. Good spot for the night before entering the park.

quebec-wild.name: 52nd avenue “cul de sac”
quebec-wild.notes: This is a dead end next to a big park with plenty of Deer.  It is big enough for 10 cars or Vans.  Pretty quiet.  No services at all, just a great place to spend the night without being hassled.  I stay here 1 day out of 2 these days, cause work is 8 minutes away.  Also no spot lights in your face like other places.

quebec-wild.name: St. Andrews
quebec-wild.notes: Parking area right near corner of King and Queen Street across from ‘Sheriff Andrews House’ . Pulled into a single row of parking spaces in van after dark and slept well. Just 75 yards away is a lovely restaurant open for breakfast ‘Station on King Eatery’ with good coffee with view of harbour. Love this town, very nice!

quebec-wild.name: End of Runway
quebec-wild.notes:
*Overnight parking/camping is NOT permitted at this location.
.....
In the end of the airport runway, there´s a rocky beach.
Can get very windy.

quebec-wild.name: Barachois Falls Trail head
quebec-wild.notes: Trail head , just a flat parking.. but very very quiet

quebec-wild.name: Lighthouse Cape Ray
quebec-wild.notes: Just before the the light house, small rough road that bring you a nice level parking.

quebec-wild.name: Pebble beach camp
quebec-wild.notes: Quiet camp below a cul-de-sac gravel road. Protected from southerly winds, large area and plenty of space. Not recommended for huge RVs (they can stay a bit further on on a pullout of the gravel road or along the way out here). View of the bay, swimming and fire making at the beach possible (bring your own wood).

quebec-wild.name: Pull out at river bank next to 510
quebec-wild.notes: Pull out of the 510  between Cartwright and Happy Valley-Goose Bay next to a bridge. The place goes down to the river bank and has a nice view.

quebec-wild.name: Basketball, Soccer Ground
quebec-wild.notes: I parked besides the basketball ground and slept inside of my van. Just a few passing vehicles because of the National Historic Site and the fantastic view on the lights of the city at night. In the morning some local people walk their dogs there. But all in all very quiet place. I saw a pit toilet but didn't check if it is available.

quebec-wild.name: River Philip
quebec-wild.notes:
T-junction of a snowmobile track.  We receive a curious local to make sure who we were.  Quiet place.

if you want to be on the side of the road, so instead of there we pulled into the foot of the bridge just before this place where you can fish or launch a kayak. It was beautiful and off the road.

quebec-wild.name: Trail end
quebec-wild.notes:
Come at the end of a little trail (Shemogue Harbour Shore Road).
Pro: Calm and isolated from the road. Just near a small beach.
Cons: Lot of mosquitoes during summer...

quebec-wild.name: Relais Gabriel
quebec-wild.notes: Nice spot on the water just off the main road. You have to go down a gravel road with some loose rocks, but we were fine with our 2WD T3 and T5 VW campers. Plenty of room for a few rigs. Spot was recommended to us by a local.

quebec-wild.name: Little Presque Isle (roadside)
quebec-wild.notes: Just off route 130. Road side spot next to stream with path down to water. No hook ups. It’s on route 103 North. 5 minutes from Hartland NB  where the longest covered bridge in the world is located. Bit of highway noise.

quebec-wild.name: Lighthouse - Fort Amherst
quebec-wild.notes:
Quiet place with a nice view. Parking lot + space for tent
You can make a fire along the coast, there's a little beach down the hill, and the forest host a nice curious fox.

quebec-wild.name: Gosling Park
quebec-wild.notes: Former Campground... abandoned. Still all sites intact, but best place is to park is directly by the lake. It’s used only once per year for a weekend in August for a Regatta.

quebec-wild.name: Pullout next to a waterfall
quebec-wild.notes: There are pullouts on both sides of a bridge by a waterfall. Directly next to the road, but not much traffic in the evening. One of the few wind sheltered spots we could find. Nice view of bay and hills across the road.

quebec-wild.name: Next to the river
quebec-wild.notes: Small, nice place with easy, but narrow access. Nice view of the river. Just for one small car or a tent.

quebec-wild.name: Knoll Spruce Road
quebec-wild.notes:
Beautiful at creek in the middle of nowhere! Plenty of room, three separate camping areas. 

Best to access this location via route 8 -> 360 -> 430 (west). The gravel road in is in great shape because of the mines located in the area. May require some clearance turning into camp area.

quebec-wild.name: Village relais Amqui Parking
quebec-wild.notes:
Small parking between the road and the railway.
One train around 8pm and another around 0h00.
Restaurant close by.
Ok for one night.

quebec-wild.name: Meat Cove Cliff
quebec-wild.notes: Large place to stay near the road but no traffic. Little bit windy. Good view of ocean. Good cell coverage from Telus and Koodo here, full bar for phone signal, data is LTE, decently fast but not LTE+, can stream up to 720p. If you go in toward Meat Cove, about 2km,  it becomes spotty and sometimes no coverage.

quebec-wild.name: The Old 132
quebec-wild.notes: A very nice place to overnight. quiet along Matapédia river. lots of place to park

quebec-wild.name: Halte Routière
quebec-wild.notes: rest area on route 117. washrooms, picnic tables, some covered. Two parking areas, with the furthest one having an area big enough for 3-4 rigs.

quebec-wild.name: Halte Routière 113 N
quebec-wild.notes: a picnic area/rest stop with dry toilet, boat ramp, picnic tables and room for 3-4 RVs .

quebec-wild.name: Black River
quebec-wild.notes: ATV trailhead right off dirt road. Nothing special but good for a night and remote enough to not be bothered

quebec-wild.name: St Georges
quebec-wild.notes: Illuminated parking on the edge of a not busy road. Picnic table and trash. Quiet night.

quebec-wild.name: Tanya Lake Trailhead
quebec-wild.notes: Parking lot for Tanya Lake that has a short hiking trail around the lake. Just on the outskirts of a subdivision, close to the highway so some noise. Nothing fancy but we stayed one night without problems.

quebec-wild.name: Sunday Hill Lookout
quebec-wild.notes: Beautiful view of lake Melville and the Mealy Mountains right before the lookout. Picnic table, garbage can and pit toilet beside. Down a bumpy gravel road but 4x4 probably not required

quebec-wild.name: Cabot Trail towards Ingonish
quebec-wild.notes: This is a nice spot right by the water just outside of Baddeck at the start of the Cabot Trail. There’s spots right off the highway but if you go a little deeper down the gravel road, there’s a nice spot to pull out. A little noisy due to highway traffic but a good spot for the night

quebec-wild.name: Old wharf
quebec-wild.notes: It's an old abandonment. Nice place by the bay. Windy but still quiet. Perfect for the night.

quebec-wild.name: Dorchester Cape
quebec-wild.notes: Lay-by next to the beach, no signs to say no overnight parking and no facilities. Just a spot next to a quiet road overlooking the beach.

quebec-wild.name: Bear pond parking
quebec-wild.notes: This is a parking use for the 4wheeler during hunting season. easy to get in al 4 seasons.

quebec-wild.name: Le Prospecteur Hiking Trails
quebec-wild.notes: Stayed one night. Parking in the Wood. Entry for pedestrian trials. Quiet and Alone after 6pm. A Wall Mart is located at 1,2km as a backup.

quebec-wild.name: Parc Optimiste
quebec-wild.notes: Parking area of a nice little park in Cap-Saint-Ignace. Very quiet, no signs against overnight parking. Garbage pick up came in the morning but didn't say anything. There were probably toilets there but they were blocked by snow. Might be busy in summer.

quebec-wild.name: Camping plage soleil couchant
quebec-wild.notes: Only in winter. Large place on the banks of Saint-Jean lake. It is snow-clear and there are also fishing huts. Beautiful place. Access just before Camping Plage Soleil Couchant.

quebec-wild.name: Coronation park
quebec-wild.notes: Alternate side of street beside residential neighborhood park. 24 hrs parking allowed. Urban street parking walking distance to Metro transit station

quebec-wild.name: Isle Madame
quebec-wild.notes: On the port at the entrance, large space in front of the harbor.

quebec-wild.name: Petit Cap Beach
quebec-wild.notes:
Nice spot, very quiet, no mud, very beautiful view on the beach. 

PLEASE TAKE YOUR GARBAGE WITH YOU!

quebec-wild.name: Forest next to abandoned road
quebec-wild.notes: Right next to a long time abandoned tarmac road, which runs through a wooded area. The wild camp area is on the northern end of road, and the only green area without tracks. Only a few hundred metres from highway 10 which is handy for an overnight stay. Pleasent, clean and quiet but no real view. Not recommended for anything more than a night stop, but beats any Walmart or gas station car park. Firm ground with shingle under it. Big rigs could fit if approaching from northern end. Other tall rigs may need to squeeze past low hanging trees if approaching from south end.

quebec-wild.name: Wilderness area next to Richibucto Road
quebec-wild.notes:
Entrance next to large electric substation, on Richibucto Road. On a old hunting line trail cross roads, near the river. Area is full of moose. This is a wilderness area managed by the new brunswick province. It has a network of old logging and hunting trails, which activities are prohibited now, including collecting firewood so bring your own. You don't necessary need to go to our spot, you can go either 500meters from Richibucto Road on a gravel road or 3 km into the bush.
Great for a half day and/or night stop over for peace and quite, hiking and cycling. 4x4 is a must if you go deep into Bush, but large or non-4x4 rigs can stay on or near the gravel entry road.
Natural water spring up the road on highway 10 which all the locals use, has tap.
Near by ww2 POW camp historical site.

quebec-wild.name: Lac Marlene
quebec-wild.notes: Crown land campsite next to this lake. Fairly quiet but next to a dirt road. Tent camping possible as well as a small trailer.

quebec-wild.name: Petit lac cayamant
quebec-wild.notes: Tough to reach sandy spit with free camping on crown land.

quebec-wild.name: Old CP Track - Adelard
quebec-wild.notes: This trail leads you to an old CP track bed just off the road. Lots of room for any size vehicle. Due to loose graveal, I recommend a 4x4 vehicle

quebec-wild.name: Old Lumber - Adelar
quebec-wild.notes: This is a great place off the highway ( 7 to 10min of trail ) Lots of options once you arrive at the clearing. If you continue north once you arrive at the clearing you will arrive at the river. ( We recommend Small to Midsize vehicle with 4x4. The trail is very simple and stock friendly )

quebec-wild.name: Old CP Track - Head, Clara and Maria
quebec-wild.notes: Just off the highway, this trail is an old maintenance trail to the CP track. You cant drive on the track bed because they put cut outs but there is room to park. Has a view of the Ottawa river. Maybe noisy since you are close to the road.

quebec-wild.name: Halte routière
quebec-wild.notes: Roadside stop -  just before reaching the toilet there is a small gravel road on the right. Take this little path that makes a loop and leads to picnic tables with a few places to park. Only for small rigs example Sprinter 21 feet. All the rest stops should have these nice places to sleep. It's all ready for a sugar shack in a maple forest. Magnificent!  --- A la halte routière juste avant d'arriver au toilette il y a un petit chemin de gravelle sur la droite. Prendre ce petit chemin qui fait une boucle et mêne à des tables de pique nique avec quelques places pour se stationner. Seulement pour des petits rigs exemple Sprinter 21 pieds. Toute les haltes routières devraient avoir de ces chouettes endroits pour y dormir. C'est tout prêt d'une cabane à sucre dans une forêts d'érables. Magnifique!

quebec-wild.name: Off TransCanada Hwy
quebec-wild.notes: There are a couple of spots for tents all around. The gps coordinates lead to a big opening with 360^ view of the forest. We can hear the cars. ---  Il y a quelques spots le long du chemin pour tentes ou véhicule. Les coordonnées gps mènent à un plateau avec vue 360^ de la forêt! On entend un peu la route.

quebec-wild.name: Connors Bros
quebec-wild.notes: Quiet place with shelter!  The square is big enough to accommodate several cars.  There is a small trail behind that will allow you to go by the sea and make a loop.

quebec-wild.name: Beside CP track.
quebec-wild.notes:
Large lot beside old CP track. Looks like local youth meets here too.

Near a gas station with restaurant and store, maybe toilets, didn't go there.

quebec-wild.name: Cap Pelé docks
quebec-wild.notes: Rough camped a night here in the off-season. I think at the height of fishing season this might be a little more active, but in early May it was pretty quiet in the morning. As long as you stay away from the buildings and talk yourself off to the side, you shouldn’t upset anybody. The road is reasonably well traveled, so parking on the gravel shoulder isn’t going to be a very restful night but if you just need a place to stop this one is excellent. There are still a few fishermen around here, so it might even be a good place to buy seafood, who knows? There is also a restaurant here that comes highly recommended by local friends. Apparently the clams are delicious!

quebec-wild.name: Port Daniel
quebec-wild.notes: Large, paved parking lot between the tourist information centre and the river.

quebec-wild.name: Halte Langue-de-chattes
quebec-wild.notes:
Very nice place, free campground offered by the municipality. ** Warning ** there is a barrier to the entrance to the road accessible only for cars under 9 feet high
.....
très belle place, terrain de camping gratuit offert par la municipalité. **Attention** il y a une entrave à l'entrée de la route accessible seulement pour les voitures de moins de 9 pieds de haut.

quebec-wild.name: Parc Pierre Brochu
quebec-wild.notes: nice place to stop for a sleep. quiet at night. On the side of the Matapedia lake. clean and roomy

quebec-wild.name: Parc des Chutes
quebec-wild.notes: Great spot, quiet, big space. No signs for no overnight, we spent 2 nights here and weren't bothered.

quebec-wild.name: gravel pit
quebec-wild.notes: a place for 4-5 véhicules, off route 117, next to bike path. No services, but good to crash.

quebec-wild.name: Lighthouse Road
quebec-wild.notes: There is no overnight parking at the Lighthouse, but there are spots along the road (on the side) for vehicles to park for the night by the shore... sunset and sunrise on the water, beautiful. We spent the night with no problems. **Keep an eye on the wind forecast, the bridge to get here is tall and gets cross winds. Big rigs could get here, but be cautious as the roads are narrow and old (I think the Lighthouse at the end of the road is the only good turn around spot.)

quebec-wild.name: Lac Dumont
quebec-wild.notes:
Back country camping overlooking the lake. Possible to drive on the lake. Lots of spots. Beware sometimes the locals will use this spot to party. 

Don't trust your GPS I got lost in the bunch with my truck

quebec-wild.name: Place by River
quebec-wild.notes: Little spot in front of a salmon river, belvédère, fire pit, pic table, trash. Quiet and nice. No sign for 'no overnight' !

quebec-wild.name: Park Gouin
quebec-wild.notes:
Parking lot. No prohibition sign. Near the rivers to the meadows. Very calm.
---
Parking. Pas d'interdiction. près de la rivières aux prairies. très calme.

quebec-wild.name: Shoal Point Beach Camping
quebec-wild.notes: Quiet and beautiful spot in the beach just outside a small community. Very friendly locals who told us is was fine to go off-road the beach and camp. They also showed us where high tide was so we’d be safe (either in grass or next to it) and shared some beer. We went through some soft sand and had to lower tire pressure. 4x4 required.

quebec-wild.name: Parc National Monts-Valin
quebec-wild.notes:
small gravel parking at the edge of the road 172. troubleshooting for one night. water on site
___
petit parking en graviers au bord de la route 172. dépannage pour une nuit. eau sur place

quebec-wild.name: Steadybrook Falls Trailhead
quebec-wild.notes: Large parking area at the base of the road going to steadybrook.

quebec-wild.name: Parking Wendaké
quebec-wild.notes:
Large car park just behind the « Institut de développement durable des Premières Nations du Québec et du Labrador ». 
No noise. Shadow on the morning. 
Near to the shopping center « les galeries de la capitale ». 
Perfect for few nights near Quebec City.

quebec-wild.name: Primitive Campsite
quebec-wild.notes: Primitive Campsite along Forest Road 403

quebec-wild.name: Large Field
quebec-wild.notes: Wild camping in large field. Area full on the weekend of the "Festival Western" the rest of the summer is free. Quiet place. OK for 1 night.

quebec-wild.name: Car pool spot
quebec-wild.notes:
Quiet car pool spot with a box for books Library. Stay a night. 
You can Boondock on the other side of the road.

quebec-wild.name: Rivière-des Outaouais
quebec-wild.notes:
Small, beautiful place close to an established campground. This place is very close to the river and sadly also very close to the road. 
Lot of fishermen use this place to launch their boat during the summer months.
There is one picnic table and no one is going to bother you if you spend the night there.
None or very poor cellular connection. Easy way in and out.

quebec-wild.name: Dozois Dam
quebec-wild.notes:
Not so quiet because of the road, but nice place to spend a night or two if you don’t want to camp a little farther north.
Great boat ramp just close by.
Beautiful lake in front and rivers on the two sides.
Great place to explore by boat or kayak.
Even good cell connection.

quebec-wild.name: Ossokmanuan Reservior
quebec-wild.notes: A large gravel pit, currently not active, but right on a small part in of the Ossokmanuan Reservoir. Drive to the very back of the site to be near the water and away from the highway.  A natural water source is close by but it is very steep from the site to the water.

quebec-wild.name: Dead end Wemotaci Road
quebec-wild.notes: Primitive Campsite on Wemotaci Road. The Trail is blocked just before the river and there’s a fire ring and place to camp. Not very spacious!

quebec-wild.name: Chemin du Chenail du Moine
quebec-wild.notes:
End of the road.  A quiet parking place with room for a few véhicules. A quiet night. Near La Maison du Marais (swamp house). Make a small contribution and take a walk along the swamp.
Park your car in their parking, use their ramp (small fee) and take a beautiful kayak ride. Restaurant with local food on the other side of the road.
Poor cell connection.

quebec-wild.name: Carheil plage/beach
quebec-wild.notes: Nice beach with room for many RV 8 KM south of town. 2 bench park and a picnic table. Garbage dumpster available. Lake is many miles long. Take Duchesneau street from Fermont drive south 7.5km on a gravel road passing some gravel pits. A few white signs on the way.

quebec-wild.name: Glencoe Mills
quebec-wild.notes: A pullout close to the Glencoe Mills Hall.  Not noteworthy in itself except it is flat and a good place to stay after attending a dance at the hall.

quebec-wild.name: Former Quarry
quebec-wild.notes: Just another spot for an overnight stay along Route 510. Out if sight from main road. Trash-free as of now. Plenty of rocks and wood for a campfire.

quebec-wild.name: Cap, pointe Auguet
quebec-wild.notes:
Beautiful spot close to the point where the lighthouse 
Trails along the coast. ..as of today be careful the road is washed away before the lighthouse :you can't make it up to it.
Super quiet also. ...there is enough space at some point on the road to turn around our 8m Sprinter

quebec-wild.name: Halte routière de St-Sylvestre
quebec-wild.notes:
Municipal stop with ecological toilet... And picnic table, located in the countryside. No ban on overnight.

Halte municipale avec toilettes écologique... Et table de picnic, située en pleine campagne. Pas d’interdiction d’overnight.

quebec-wild.name: Centre de loisir Charles Valence
quebec-wild.notes:
Notre Dame-Des-Bois Church
Large parking West of the Church, fairly level, quiet, closes to Mont-Mégantic observatory

quebec-wild.name: Next the road
quebec-wild.notes: The first free place we found on this road. Next the road at the end of the gravel road. No service but free and quiet!

quebec-wild.name: Rivière-du-loup
quebec-wild.notes:
Parking spot no services side road view of the st-Lawrence.

Stationnement pas de service rue tranquille vue du st-laurent.

quebec-wild.name: Blue beach
quebec-wild.notes: A small fishing wharf at the end of a 10 km gravel road, at the tip of the point

quebec-wild.name: Humber Valley Trailhead
quebec-wild.notes: Gravel parking for the Humber Valley Trail (a part of the International Appalachian Trail).

quebec-wild.name: Point au Mal Beach
quebec-wild.notes: Beach road on a barachois. Superbs views on the surroundings

quebec-wild.name: entrée parc Jacques Cartier
quebec-wild.notes:
big parking just before Jacques Cartier national Park. A bit noisy with the highway.

Grand parking juste avant l'entrée du parc de la Jacques Cartier, un peu bruyant avec l'autoroute à côté.

quebec-wild.name: Old 132 road
quebec-wild.notes: This is the old road for the 132. There are a number of places to stop overnight along the road, some with picnic tables. If one place is occupied just roll on to the next. Very little traffic. You can have fires. There is a lively river that runs along this road. It is accessible  to the main 132 from both ends. The water available is from a stream/spring, clean but no hose connection.

quebec-wild.name: Massif du Sud sentier
quebec-wild.notes: site belong to the Massif du Sud but you can spend the night without problem. There’s a dry toilet. At 5 minutes you have access to a river and hiking trails.

quebec-wild.name: Halte L’Iris
quebec-wild.notes: Roadside picnic area just off hi way 55 Southbound . 3 picnic tables and gravel parking lot. Would be ok for a night. Just passing through and stopped for lunch.

quebec-wild.name: Viewpoint
quebec-wild.notes: Great place to spend the night if it is not to windy - beautiful view of the bay of Saint Paul and the whole surrounding. Picknick table, trash bin and a million stars at night.

quebec-wild.name: macintyre lake
quebec-wild.notes: Nice site on lake, paved and level. Road in is short but overgrown and very narrow. Only suitable for camper vans or truck campers. Room for 2 or 3 rigs. The train tracks next to the site are not in use anymore.

quebec-wild.name: Riviere Louvicourt
quebec-wild.notes:
First road across the bridge.
There is room for a few campers.
There are no facilities but a picnic table is available.
Close to the main road but since it is a 50 km zone, there is little noise.
Good cellular phone coverage.

quebec-wild.name: Frye island
quebec-wild.notes: Wild camping on beach. Camp at top of beach to avoid getting wet at high tide. Owned by conservation society, practice LNT

quebec-wild.name: Road 113
quebec-wild.notes: Spot just out of the road 113 for Chibougamau on the right side. At the beginning of a secondary road. Not easy to be out of the trafic in this area.

quebec-wild.name: Halte municipale de Notre-Dame-des-Bois
quebec-wild.notes: Quiet rest area with a beautiful view of Mont-Mégantic.

quebec-wild.name: Rivière Opinaca
quebec-wild.notes:
Located at KM 411 on James Bay Road
View of the river.
This is a place to sleep not a campsite.
There are picnic tables and some fire rings.
Room for about 10 campers.
No service.

quebec-wild.name: Lighthouse - Cape Ray
quebec-wild.notes:
Update Oct 2022: gravel road is washed out post-hurricane Fiona. I have added updated photos of the current gravel road conditions. You could still walk down and tent it but I can't see anything other than an ATV making it around the washed-out area. 
.....
Drive down the gravel road at the lighthouse, lovely flat spot close by the beach. Check the road before driving down, it is steep and has big potholes from other 4x2 trying to come back up.

quebec-wild.name: Louvicourt tower
quebec-wild.notes:
A lot of place for wild camping around here. Place for big rig and tent. 
Take the Telebec Louvicourt trail and drive 100m
Plusieurs place et petit chemin forestier pour camping sauvage.
Prendre le chemin Telebec Louvicourt et faire 100m

quebec-wild.name: Réservoir La Grande-1
quebec-wild.notes: Large boat ramp with easy access and beautiful view of the water.

quebec-wild.name: Pontbriand river lookout
quebec-wild.notes: You can drive by the river down the lookout. Close from the road but quiet.

quebec-wild.name: St Leonard
quebec-wild.notes: Big space right before the usa border. Turn left just before the border gate. River view

quebec-wild.name: La Baie park
quebec-wild.notes: Small area to park. near the ottawa river. nice city view and you can meet some ducks. no bins, no toilets, no water. ok for bigs rigs. no "no camping" signs

quebec-wild.name: Chisasibi
quebec-wild.notes:
Hotel parking lot
 Recommended place for overnight parking by a local policeman.
Well lit and hydro is available on parking lights.

quebec-wild.name: Moulin à Baude
quebec-wild.notes:
Nice little spit for small vehicles, quiet. Direction: take the old road on the right when coming from Tadoussac on highway 138, and then keep an eye on the right.

One big rig might fit, but turning would be a tight challenge and better just head to the other gravel parking nearby and leave this small spot to this smaller cars.

quebec-wild.name: Terrain de sport
quebec-wild.notes: parking and space with grass next to a sport field.  no banned sign

quebec-wild.name: Stephensville Crossing Bridge
quebec-wild.notes: Vague area near the road with many spots to park among the grassy dunes.

quebec-wild.name: just before the point
quebec-wild.notes: we arrive at the point but peoples where there we decide to leave them alone and come back 1000 foots.  beautiful and quiet place.  nous avons été a la pointe mais des gens y etaient déjà, nous avons decide de revenir 1000 pieds en arrière et l'endroit est parfait et tranquille.

quebec-wild.name: Grand Bay road turnout
quebec-wild.notes:
Turn out at the side of the road. Big enough for my pickup truck and small trailer. Scenic view. Great sunset.

Road traffic earlier in the evening, especially when the ferry arrived. But after 10pm it was pretty quiet.

Mosquitoes were out.

Great cell reception.

Perfect for waiting for the ferry.

quebec-wild.name: Cape Spencer Hilltop
quebec-wild.notes:
Nice place on top of the hill, overlooking a lake, the Port in St. John and the sea.

Road from the St. John side is muddy, when wet. I don’t know about the other direction. Space for one Vehicle, maybe two.

There are easy and challenging routes into camp. Keep an eye out for brush and ledge hazards.

I had Verizon cell signal.

quebec-wild.name: Next to water
quebec-wild.notes: Ok for sleep. It's a local water access. Big rigs 30ft plus is not very good the sand sinks a bit. We have 26 and was all good.

quebec-wild.name: Sunrise Diner/gas station *Abandoned*
quebec-wild.notes: Abandoned business (there are a few on this road, businesses and old churches). Used by truckers... lots of room to park and grass for dogs.

quebec-wild.name: the giant firepit
quebec-wild.notes:
Nice wild camp at the lake, not for big rigs. Huge Firepit, shady, nice view over the lake

Fyi, the name is overselling. There's just a regular size fire pit.

quebec-wild.name: End of Wharf road near beach
quebec-wild.notes: Room for a few camper vans. Beach access possible with vehicle but beach rocky. We were the only ones there during the night. Quiet. Some fishermen and bathers during the day. Beautiful view of the Minas Bassin.

quebec-wild.name: Soccer Field
quebec-wild.notes:
Flat parking lot next to soccer field.
Quiet and a nice place to sleep.

quebec-wild.name: Lac Murray
quebec-wild.notes: Super beautiful camp spot. Only accessible from south.

quebec-wild.name: camp windigo
quebec-wild.notes: This is a nice open old camp with a lot of place

quebec-wild.name: Steadybrook Ski Field
quebec-wild.notes:
Huge carpark, empty in summer obviously.
No size limit.
Huge access.
Short walk to Tim Horton's and a beautiful waterfall.
Right on the side of the highway for access but not too close to keep you awake. 
Great scenery and moose prints on the floor outside our rig.

quebec-wild.name: Rest Area
quebec-wild.notes:
Ville de Gagnon. Large pull out. 
Plenty of room for big rigs.
Flat.
Rubbish bins but still lots of rubbish lying around. 

Typical truck pull in. Ok if you need a place to sleep. 

If you're looking for a nice spot and have a smaller rig say <20ft or 4wd, about 500m north of this spot there is a rough track leading down to some lovely lake front spots.  Just down the bank from the signs telling the story of the old town.

quebec-wild.name: Rivière Papinachois
quebec-wild.notes:
Permission need it from Passamit community! 

Multiple spot for tents and RV near the rapids of Papinachois river

quebec-wild.name: Rivière Mistassibi
quebec-wild.notes: A peaceful place, on the edge of the Mistassibi River, it is a large field, unserviced and available with a magnificent sunrise.

quebec-wild.name: New Brunswick NR
quebec-wild.notes: Natural Resources - New Brunswick. This place is very calm, not much traffic. You have beautiful view on the Bay. There is a trash can. But nothing else.

quebec-wild.name: Old road port Phillip
quebec-wild.notes: There is an old road next to the actual one. the road ends here, because the bridge is demolished.

quebec-wild.name: Parc de la Baie
quebec-wild.notes:
Large gravel parking lot behind Parc de la Baie. Across the street from a lovely bike and pedestrian path along the Ottawa river. 

Nice restaurants nearby. View of Ottawa.
---
Parking calme et tranquille pour la nuit. Restaurant sympa à côté. Très belle vue sur Ottawa. Marche piétonnier et quai tout près.

quebec-wild.name: Clowns Island
quebec-wild.notes: After passing in a 4×4 trail, you'll pass near a river. There is an island on the other side of that river where you can install your tent. Sure, you'll need to cross the river with your stock over your head, but in the end, this spot is amazing and incredebly relaxing.

quebec-wild.name: Ginger Route Trailhead
quebec-wild.notes: Parking lot at the trailhead with a picnic table and trash bin. It's less than one kilometre from the RV dump at the local visitor info centre.

quebec-wild.name: old docks
quebec-wild.notes: old docks next to a park that is now used by the fishermans. lots of locals go there to enjoy the view so please don’t roll up with a 30ft bus

quebec-wild.name: Parc des Artistes
quebec-wild.notes: Municipal park. Rivière éternité. Parc des artistes. Toilet open all day. There were no places left at the provincial park. They suggested we spend the night here. Central fire place and picnic tables. Fridge available

quebec-wild.name: Parking Route 138
quebec-wild.notes:
Giant 24h parking advertised from rt138.
green toilet equipped with light.
4 picnic tables under wooden roof.
close to rt 138 but not that noisy and you can see the entrance clearly.

quebec-wild.name: Chip & Chap hill
quebec-wild.notes: if you don't like all the boat launching action over the street, here you can have your solitude and peace. you still hear the road but much less than on the other side . a lot of chipmunks came to say hello.

quebec-wild.name: Deer Lake Car Park
quebec-wild.notes: A free car park in the entrance of the town by the power station, a bit noisy as it is by the main road and near the plant, but suitable for a night stop. There is a beach with locals swimming next to it a fisherman. No amenities.

quebec-wild.name: Rivière aux Tonnerres 2
quebec-wild.notes: on the 138 road, just after Riviere aux Tonnerres town, at right when you go to  the East

quebec-wild.name: Hills river boat ramp parking lot
quebec-wild.notes: Great waterfront site. Level gravel parking lot with no road noise and good privacy. Cell service is great. No services.

quebec-wild.name: Route 431
quebec-wild.notes: Pin isn’t in the right place! But it’s a really cool spot on the beach with mountains surrounding. Couple fire pits, a broken down bus. Leave no trace.  Wonderful spot by the lake. Down a gravel road far enough from the main road and well hidden. Plenty of room for a few campers, and bigger area just before the lake.  Big vehicles and big RVs can turn but be prepared for many pot holes. No service.

quebec-wild.name: Huntington point
quebec-wild.notes: At end of dead end dirt road. Near some cottages. Quiet, clean location. No services. 25 ft from stone beach.

quebec-wild.name: Darling Long Boat Launch
quebec-wild.notes: Access is along a maintained road but high clearance vehicle needed. Site is a bit rocky, but there are a few tent sites. Decent water for a swim.

quebec-wild.name: Information side of the road
quebec-wild.notes:
Pull in parking on the side of the road for information signe. Quiet even if its on the road side.

Place en bord route, tranquille. Difficile d’etre de niveau mais tres accessible en vr.

quebec-wild.name: St-Peters National Historic Site
quebec-wild.notes:
This is opposite to Battery Provincial Park on the other side of the canal.
I guess we could have stayed on the parking down the hill near the water (and actually on the St-Peters National Historic Site), but we did not feel comfortable. We instead climb up the hill and found this small dirt and grassy parking near the St-Peters Coastal Trail.
In theory, we would have a nice view on the water from this higher point, but bushes and small trees obstruct the view, at least from the RV. You can walk to the edge of the hill though to get a nice view.
It was quiet. There was another RV (kind of a 4x4 high clearance monster RV) when we were there, but nobody in it.
We were in a camper van. It is not big-rig-friendly, but I guess a small trailer could stay there as well.

quebec-wild.name: Jemseg - Community Park
quebec-wild.notes: Small, well-maintained park. I parked behind the white building which gives almost complete privacy from the road.

quebec-wild.name: End of Fisherman’s Harbor Lake
quebec-wild.notes: Small gravel driveway leads to an opening by the lakeshore. Not recommended for big rigs but fine for a 24’ sprinter. Beautiful view by the lake. Quiet.

quebec-wild.name: Hunter's Point (Private property)
quebec-wild.notes: At the point of the site.  This place is own by a very nice lady.  She was more than willing to let my family of 5 in 2 SUV to used her land and use the access to the lake.

quebec-wild.name: Chute Sainte-Anne Firepit
quebec-wild.notes:
There's a small clearing by the river here with a firepit. Drive up to Chemin De La Rivière to the very end (which doesn't prohibit overnight parking) and walk in 1km along the river. Once the trail starts to get really rough with fallen trees (subject to change), you will find the campsite hidden against a ridge between the trail and the river. If you see the giant landslide across the river, you just passed it by a few meters.

There is access to fresh water here. Somewhat stoney. Definitely tent camping only since you have to hike in. No amenities.

quebec-wild.name: Slack's cove
quebec-wild.notes: almost at the end of lower rockport road. just past the slack's cove monument. rough dirt road passable with 2wd, ground clearance necessary. very quiet.  some camps nearby. popular spot for locals for bonfires and playing on the mud flats.

quebec-wild.name: Wild spot
quebec-wild.notes: Nice isolated spot. A few km from the main highway through a gravel road. The place is very big but the access requires high clearance or 4x4. No cell signal.

quebec-wild.name: Judes Point
quebec-wild.notes: A great spot at or on the beach, depends if you are 2wd or 4x4. access is ease of main road direct to beach side. outstanding place.

quebec-wild.name: Halte routière Municipalité de Frontenac
quebec-wild.notes:
Pretty, clean with chemical toilets clean picnic tables and some fireplaces. The road is relatively close and can be noisy. 
--
Jolie, propre avec toilettes chimiques tables de picnic propres et quelques foyers. La route est relativement proche et peut être bruyante.

quebec-wild.name: Waterloo Municipal Rest Area
quebec-wild.notes: Simple rest area, quiet even during the day.

quebec-wild.name: halte rivière rupert
quebec-wild.notes: Large parking with table picnic and bathroom and garbage

quebec-wild.name: baie James
quebec-wild.notes: you have  2 spot with table picnic and garbage  and large parking too ...cell signal available

quebec-wild.name: beach public
quebec-wild.notes:
a lot of place to park for the night  and if you want you can go swim at the beach....To cool for me :) 
cell Phone service available

quebec-wild.name: River View
quebec-wild.notes: Great little spot by the river. Not a lot of space but good for 2 vehicles. Fire ring

quebec-wild.name: Matawin River Beach
quebec-wild.notes:
Amazing spot along Forest Road 1451, right on the beach and lot of space but very narrow steep downhill to access. I give 4.5/5 because it’s just beside the road but not heavy traffic here !!   

The beach is often flooded under water, so make sure to go only when the river water level is low. There is also no bridge across the river to the south (it was torn down years ago), so do not attempt get there by going through the Mastigouche Wildlife Reserve.

quebec-wild.name: Rest stop
quebec-wild.notes: Observation area next highway. Ok to stay one night. Has picnic tables and a nice view on mountains. No sign “no over-night”, but noisy.

quebec-wild.name: Camping spot at the river
quebec-wild.notes: This is a nice camping spot for travellers without a vehicle. Perfect for those who took the ferry and need a place to sleep. It's quite difficult to find a flat and not stony place to pitch a tent but not impossible. The place is hidden from the road because it's downhill, we spent here a calm night because the road seemed to be not used a lot. When you get downhill turn right and go almost to the end,  that's where we found our spot. There is a chance to be seen from the nearby house but we had no problem with it.

quebec-wild.name: Quai Grosse île Pier
quebec-wild.notes:
Parking for fishing boats. 4x4 can go on the beaches after septembre 15. Nice view.  No service. Lunch shack open in summer. Good sea food!
Stationnement en gravier pour les bateaux de pêches. Les 4x4 peuvent aller sur la plage après le 15 septembre. Belle vue de la mer. Restaurant de fruit de mer avec terrasse ouvert l'été. Aucun service.

quebec-wild.name: Neighbourhood parking
quebec-wild.notes:
Neighbourhood parking for free. 24hrs, but no parking on Thursdays. Different streets in this area have a different day for no parking.

Café 500 m away. Park is 100 m away.

quebec-wild.name: Miminegash Harbor
quebec-wild.notes: Very large, very active lobstering Harbor parking lot-50 large new lobster boats tied up when we arrived(4PM), all gone by 6AM the following morning! Very friendly and helpful fisherman, just find a spot where you’ll be out of the way(many options). A small gas station and convenience store are a few hundred yards away. The coastal portion of Rt. 14 is a beautiful drive.

quebec-wild.name: Beach / lake camp
quebec-wild.notes:
Flat open grassy hill on the beach. Overlooking a lake. Few fire pits. Room for big rigs.  Gravel road in for about 2 km. Wide and easy going. No 4wd required.   

Gate near end. Was open when I came.

quebec-wild.name: Cliff top camping
quebec-wild.notes:
Camping spot upon the cliff, overlooking the ocean. Nice elevated view. Room for 1 - 2 vehicles.  No fire pits / facilities.  

Follow gravel road towards coast. The final section is a loop road which goes to the site. One section of the loop road is quite overgrown, but you don’t need to use that section (go back the way you came).

No 4wd required. We managed with a 2wd van, high clearance. Biggest issue is mud.
