Petit espace/parking deux places situé en haut de la marina + plage de Shigawake. Bel endroit pour un feu.

quebec-wild.name: Gare Labelle
quebec-wild.notes: Free parking close to hiking trails. Next to "le train du nord" trails. Bathroom and restaurant close by.

quebec-wild.name: Waterside beach N
quebec-wild.notes:
There is a 100m road to 2 gravel parking spots off the road and leading to the sea. Someone from Moncton confirmed it is crown. 

The road is quite bumpy and has some deep holes - lopsided at times too. I would recommend 4x4 because you might bottom out your car. 

Past the stream is the second gravel parking spot with east access to the beach. Sand and the change of times is incredible!

quebec-wild.name: Nouvelle centre sportif
quebec-wild.notes:
Small quiet place behind the trailers,
No toilet, no noise, stay discreet

Petit endroit tranquille en arrière des remorques , 
Aucune toilette, aucun bruit , restez discret

quebec-wild.name: Flea Market
quebec-wild.notes: Allow people to sleep overnight. Market is open on weekend.

quebec-wild.name: Off Main Road
quebec-wild.notes:
Nice spot just off the "main road"
Easy access with a regular 4-door car.
Black flies and dragon flies central. Watch for turtles all along this road.

quebec-wild.name: Scotstown
quebec-wild.notes:
At the side of the water near a dam. Beautiful place. Attention: near to a railway line, No signage prohibiting camping. 
.....
 Au bord de l’eau près d’un barrage. Endroit magnifique. Attention! Près d’une voie ferrée. Aucun symbole de no camping.

quebec-wild.name: Pont d'Aluminium
quebec-wild.notes: Parking for the Saguenay pathway. Please leave no trace.

quebec-wild.name: South Hampton Parish
quebec-wild.notes: This is an old park, with nice flat ground for tents or vans/RVs and lots of trees, with a look out of the river! Nice quiet spot across from a cemetery!

quebec-wild.name: Petit Anse dead end road
quebec-wild.notes: This is at the end of a dead end residential ocean front road, very beautiful. big enough for one or 2 cars or one RV / trailer. After we parked a truck / trailer showed up and left. while technically there is enough room, it wouldn't be advisable to park more than one.

quebec-wild.name: Cheticamp causeway pullout
quebec-wild.notes: There are a couple of pullouts on the ocean side of the causeway between Cheticamp and Cheticamp Island, room for a few small rigs or one larger, but not huge rigs. View and sound of the waves! Very quiet at night, cars go by during the day and into the evening. 3 bars of Telus.

quebec-wild.name: Street Parking
quebec-wild.notes: Parallel parked on the gravel side street next to Tim Hortons. walked and shopped / ate at the local business. Was a good day / evening. oh it also has a beautiful view of the lighthouse and ocean!

quebec-wild.name: Parking Lot
quebec-wild.notes:
Quiet place to pass the night. Room for several vehicles.
.....
Stationnement de la piste cyclable de Bellechasse, une douzaine de places…. Endroit tranquille pour passer la nuit pour petits VR

quebec-wild.name: Refuge Capuccin
quebec-wild.notes: Not far from a regional forest and capuccin refuge. A recent forest cut and forest road that leads into it.  About 200m from the main road on a rough but hard path. It is quiet and not many cars on main road.  I think we can turn around our car and 18ft trailer but it will take a bit of caution if you have very low clearance.

quebec-wild.name: Saint Donat, Parc des Pionniers
quebec-wild.notes: The police told us to stay overnight here (as opposed to trailhead parkinglots). There are currently signs no camping but we noticed several other RVs. It must be part of new regulations in St Donat allowing overnight stays at this designated spot. The details are on the municipal website according to police. The site is quite nice and large, it seems quiet and close to the beach.

quebec-wild.name: Roadside
quebec-wild.notes: amazing spot along troutspawn lake road. established firepit, a little tricky to get down the steep sandy and slightly uneven ramp but if you can, it's worth it! Large enough for several vehicles. not much cell coverage. if you can't make it in, there are two firepits established on the main road. the road is extremely easy to travel!

quebec-wild.name: Riverside spots
quebec-wild.notes: Just to the north-side of the signs about the old mining town, look for a very short dirt-trail down to the riverside. There are several areas open and flat. Lovely views of the river and not much road noise. Its a bit rough to get down there, but most overlanding rigs and vans should make it without problem. Plenty of space for larger rigs, just walk it first to check that your vehicle could make it down okay (and back up in the morning!). No facilities. Free.

quebec-wild.name: Timber lake #2
quebec-wild.notes: specific location of 2nd site, details already provided in other post.

quebec-wild.name: Capstick Beach
quebec-wild.notes: Going to Meat Cove a road leading down to Capstick Beach with enough for a small-medium rig, we had a van. Not suitable for trailers. Bottom area is off-level as well. Can be a tight turnaround at bottom and though the road is short and good it is slightly steeper at the bottom and has the potential to be muddy. I wouldn't use if really wet and maybe walk down first to see if it works for you. nice view of the rocky Beach and loud waves all night. Leave it cleaner than how you found it please.

quebec-wild.name: Small Pullout
quebec-wild.notes: Small pullout on dirt logging road, big enough for a car/truck or smaller van. Closest pullout to Kauzmann trail.

quebec-wild.name: The Quarry
quebec-wild.notes: Large abandon and flooded quarry. Not posted, locals camp for extended stays. Caution on the entrance. Lots of ruts.

quebec-wild.name: Tomifobia bicycle path
quebec-wild.notes:
Parking to access bicycle path.
Very quiet.
With a picnic table, no toilet, no water.
There is place for 2 or 3 van.

quebec-wild.name: Boat port
quebec-wild.notes: No longer functional boat port along the water, no signs for no camping. Beautiful views.

quebec-wild.name: Quad trail
quebec-wild.notes: Quad trail off of highway 28 just past the bridge on the left hand side coming out of Bancroft. Made a little campsite about 400yards off of the highway. Made it in no problem with my Tacoma. Wouldn’t recommend anything bigger.

quebec-wild.name: Former Granite Blast Site
quebec-wild.notes: Beautiful old granite quarry with flat ground. And cell service , two track remote road to get in but no need for 4wd. Big turn around space. Great spot for bouldering. Lots of shot gun shells, and active hunting.

quebec-wild.name: Muskrat falls camp site
quebec-wild.notes:
Nice large level lot to park multiple campers with $13,000,000,000.00 view!  If you park in the back Western corner, there is a nice view of the large reservoir. It is a short walk to see the hydro dam. We had the place to ourselves while camping here in  mid October. There was a friendly black fox who have us company at the evening fire. 

 There is LTE cell service too.

quebec-wild.name: Under power lines
quebec-wild.notes:
Under power lines, 2 bars lte, quite the drive but Dodge caravan made it.
Not too far from highway.

quebec-wild.name: Verdun, Champlain blvd street parking
quebec-wild.notes: Along park and canal, 24 hrs street parking, safe location

quebec-wild.name: Behind IGA in Shawinigan
quebec-wild.notes:
Entrance from Boul Royal, just behind the IGA, there’s a board indicating: RV PARKING / stationnement pour VR.
Next to a park, public pool.
Quiet and close to some shops.

quebec-wild.name: Lac-Pythonga
quebec-wild.notes: Great little spot to stay by the lake. Also close to the highway, so may have some road noise. No amenities so please take your garbage with you.

quebec-wild.name: Log Chute Trailhead
quebec-wild.notes: This is a trailhead parking lot for the nearby log chute trail. It is just a gravel lot, no facilities, but is well off the main highway (35) and is quiet. There are picnic tables, garbage cans and an outhouse 200 m down the road at the log chute area. A sign in this lot says there's a 72 hour parking limit.

quebec-wild.name: Off Aylen Lake Road
quebec-wild.notes: If the access point just up the road is busy, this does in a pinch. Crown land just off the paved Aylen Lake Road, the approach to an old and unused logging road. You can still hear and see the road from here but it's fairly tucked away. Not very level or large so I would only bring one vehicle back here, no room to turn around.

quebec-wild.name: Glebe Park
quebec-wild.notes: A dirt parking lot for Glebe Park, the sculpture forest and the local museum. There are no "no parking" signs and it is very quiet back here, almost no traffic because the road dead ends at the park. There is an outhouse in the park as well.

quebec-wild.name: Digdeguash River
quebec-wild.notes: A small site just off the highway on an old abandoned road with an abandoned bridge. The view is spectacular, the highway is slightly close so every once in awhile, you could hear a transfer truck. But, if you're in a car or an RV of some sort the noise won't bother you at all. Tent campers MIGHT have more difficulty there just for the noise. But the view truly makes up for any type of noise

quebec-wild.name: Lions Lookout
quebec-wild.notes: It seems you can park overnight ONLY from Saturday night to Sunday. Good for Cars and Campervans. Pet Friendly. Go all the way to the top. No signage at all about parking on the lookout.

quebec-wild.name: Digdeguash River Abandoned Bridge
quebec-wild.notes:
A beautiful spot under the Digdeguash river abandoned bridge. Half of the bridge still stands on ground and just pillars remain across the river. 
The spot is close to the highway but still very secluded, couldn't even hear it in the SUV. Sits on a very calm and quiet cove. Ideal for vanlife and mid-size RV. There are maybe a couple tent spots but we didn't try them. 
At the end of Spur No 2 road is the bridge. The gravel road to the right will take you to spot.

quebec-wild.name: parc sanctuaire
quebec-wild.notes:
very quiet place for the night with bins and chemical toilets.
seems safe. the walkers arrive early in the morning
nice place for a night

quebec-wild.name: Parking lot
quebec-wild.notes:
Moderator Note: Please obey the restrictions as per the signage.
.....
$9 for 24hr, overnight parking. 
No trailers or RVs, STEALTH car camping only.

quebec-wild.name: Street Parking
quebec-wild.notes: Rue Champlain. Stealth car or van camping only. Residential street. Permits only for overnight parking and 60 minutes parking from 9am-7pm. Beautiful sunset and quiet street. Occasional car and bus traffic.

quebec-wild.name: Botsford street
quebec-wild.notes:
This spot is just off the main street near the restaurants and pubs! Overnight street parking is widely available in the area! 

Parking is free until 7:45 am. there are also several parking lots that may offer the same. in the winter, overnight street parking is only offered conditionally. Please check the city of monitor's website. map attached shows overnight parking. it's extremely quiet sleeping here on a Wednesday, but starts to get noisy around 7 or 8 am. the church immediately beside this particular spot rings their bell pretty loud around 9:30.

for live music che k out the Olde triangle or st. James gate, a few minutes walk from here

quebec-wild.name: Stealth residential street parking
quebec-wild.notes: Quiet street, overnight parking permitted. Close to downtown.

quebec-wild.name: Louisdale Oldman boat ramp
quebec-wild.notes: Big parking lot along the water, very quiet

quebec-wild.name: Rest Area - Route 137
quebec-wild.notes:
Small rest area close to a road but very quiet. There is also a dry toilet and few picnic tables. 

Slept one night here and it was perfect

quebec-wild.name: Sand Bank
quebec-wild.notes:
There's a grassy clearing atop the bluff, overlooking the ocean.  There is an established fire pit  and room for maybe three tents comfortably. 
The gravel road, that reaches to within 25m of the clearing, is accessible by car, if moving slowly. 
Enough room to turn around at the road end,  or atop the hill,  120m back from the end. 
Strongly recommend against trailer access,  but a really nice spot to tent on the bluff or truck camp at the road's end.
From the left side of the clearing,  there's a rope to help you back up the steep trail to access the rocky beach below.

quebec-wild.name: Dead End Luskville Falls
quebec-wild.notes: Nice place for one night or two. Not a campground. But if you drive down to the dead end there is enough room for a campervan to park up for the night right next to the entrance to the trail to Luskville Falls. No amenities, bins or toilets so you need to be self contained. We had a 170 extended Sprinter, no space for big rigs though. No signs saying you cannot park there for the night. Quiet in the day and night. Not sure if its much busier in the Summer. Trail is a really nice hike!

quebec-wild.name: Clearing off skidoo trail
quebec-wild.notes:
Secluded cleared area at the end of a road about 300m off the autoroute 347. In the winter, AWD recommended as it’s an elevated climb. Next to a sentier nationale for snow machines (skidoos) but we never heard any pass by. No signs at entrance of road other than hunting season warning, and it seems to be part of the Matawinie regional park. At the clearing, nothing but trees and nature. Low LTE signal. Path was cleared from last snow dump and no one ever came by. 
A few good hiking spots within 5-10 kms of here, or even right off this path.

quebec-wild.name: Lac Blais
quebec-wild.notes:
Translation:Free camp with access to water. Can fish here. Descent for rowboat.Pets are allowed.

Accès à l'eau. Peux y pêcher. Descente pour chaloupe. 

Droit aux chiens.

quebec-wild.name: Forrest
quebec-wild.notes: Forrest everywhere with some open areas. Road is big and made for woodtruks, but not in best conditions so don't do ist with a big camper. No Problems with 4x4. Possibility for camping every km, no Houses around so realy wild. Some cows walking around free. Good to leave the busy National-Park behind ;)

quebec-wild.name: Big parking lot
quebec-wild.notes:
Big gravel parking lot in industrial street.

Wooded area 

Very quiet

quebec-wild.name: Station de ski Massif du sud
quebec-wild.notes:
***All amenities available during ski season only (wifi-toilets-restaurant-water).***
This spot is located in the ski centre parking lot. It is very beautiful and quiet. During the ski season (from december to april), the lodge is open from 8 am to late pm and there are washroom as well as a restaurant and bar (open at 10 am). There are many hicking trails to use around in summer and winter.
/
***Toutes les installations sont disponibles durant la saison de ski seulement (eau-toilettes-wifi-resto)***
Ce site est situé dans le stationnement du centre de ski. C'est tres tranquille et avec magnifique vue. chalet est ouvert durant la saison de ski (décembre à avril), a partir de 8 am jusqu'en fin pm, il y a des toilettes et un resto-bar qui lui ouvre à 10 am. Plusieurs randonnées sont accessibles en hiver ainsi qu'en été.

quebec-wild.name: Gloocap landing, sortie 8A sur la 101
quebec-wild.notes: Very large parking lot, Tim Hortons open 24 hours, picnic table --- Très grand stationnement, Tim Horton ouvert 24h, table à pique nique, propane

quebec-wild.name: Gravel parking ocean view
quebec-wild.notes: Nice big informal parking on the side of the 138. Beautiful view on the Saint-Laurent. Little fire pit and a lot of place!

quebec-wild.name: Sentier de l’Estrie, zone Sutton
quebec-wild.notes: Small parking lot with 2 spaces leading into walking paths. There are no "No parking" signs. Very calm.

quebec-wild.name: End of the road
quebec-wild.notes: Cottage country end of the road turn around. Very quiet. There’s a dirt road that continues up and around into what appears to be a hydro cut. Would likely need a 4x4, I didn’t follow the dirt road. At this time a construction company is using part of this road end for vehicle storage and a dirt pile, but they’re not here after 4pm. There are no “no parking” signs.

quebec-wild.name: big dirt parking near beautiful lake view
quebec-wild.notes: Flat and dirt parking lot with couple of workers cabin around but further on the left you can find a nice quiet place near lake with fire pit.

quebec-wild.name: parc Victoria
quebec-wild.notes: Nice quiet place by the park.  No parking Monday to Friday between 7h and 17h.  Other than that, no other sign.

quebec-wild.name: Halte municipale
quebec-wild.notes: Perfect little spot for lunch and no signs forbidding over night stays, next to road though and noisy. Picnic tables and dry toilet

quebec-wild.name: Sand pit near old warf
quebec-wild.notes: Small trail that ends in a sandy/rocky pit. Ok for 2wd, windy. Take red road on map picture.

quebec-wild.name: Three Rock Cove
quebec-wild.notes: Nice sand pit by the Three Rock Cove. mostly protected by the wind.  Please be respectful.

quebec-wild.name: The end of 138
quebec-wild.notes: We have been shown this place by the local of fort. this is at the end of the 138 by a lake.

quebec-wild.name: sand pit close to hydro site
quebec-wild.notes: sand pit close to a hydro site. there can be alot of light from the tower.

quebec-wild.name: Ville de Gagnon
quebec-wild.notes: here is where used to be a town of 4000 people for the mining in the region. there is a back road next to it.you can sleep by the river. small rigs

quebec-wild.name: Lakeside
quebec-wild.notes: This spot has no signage of overnights being banned. Toilets are locked at night and you use a buzzer to unlock. Benches, fire pit, and a nice lookout spot. I had my Jetta with my teardrop and was able to use two spaces. I wouldn’t park here with anything bigger. Park at the top of the hill for best view!

quebec-wild.name: Lac Simon
quebec-wild.notes:
Rest stop with picnic table on the road surrounding Lac Simon (sign reads "2000 LS). No "no overnight" signs. Room for 2 or 3 small RVs. Beautiful view from top of mountain. Very quiet.
--
Halte routière avec table à pique-nique sur le chemin longeant le Lac Simon (une pancarte indique 2000 LS). Aucune interdiction d'y passer la nuit. Assez grand pour 2 ou 3 petits VR. Très tranquille. Superbe vue au lever du haut de la montagne.

quebec-wild.name: carrefour emilie de lanoraie

parking behind the church, municipal swimming pool nearby, local market in the park on weekends, park in the parking space, do not sit in the grass

parking derriere l eglise , picine municipale a proximité , marché local au parc la fin de semaine , stationner dans l espace de stationnement , ne pas s installer dans l herbe

quebec-wild.name: sand spot behind abandon sport field

to get there go at the end of the dead end there a sand trail it clear high and wide enough for a camper and smaller.
keep the place clean and peaceful please so people could keep coming here .

quebec-wild.name: Nice Picnic area next to the road
quebec-wild.notes: Great, large picnic area next to the road so it is a bit loud, but great for an overnight stop. Beautiful lake with otters, and we had a visitor from a fox. No amenities

quebec-wild.name: Gouin Reservoir
quebec-wild.notes: Wilderness camping is permitted on any of the islands in this reservoir, there are plenty of beautiful sand beaches. I will point out a specific one I stayed at and had a great experience. Good walleye/pike fishing.

quebec-wild.name: portage off route 105
quebec-wild.notes: in front of Mataquac provincial parc. right next to the St John River. place for plenty of rvs. no no parking sign. easy access to water and right off route 105. a Little bit of Grass for tents.

quebec-wild.name: Wild Camping near Alma

On a trouvé cet endroit via le satellite. Proche de la route, aucune indication pour interdire le station ou l’overnight.

quebec-wild.name: Street Parking
quebec-wild.notes: We were looking for Wifi and found out you can have it while parking in front of the  Ross Memorial Public Library on King Street. The street is quiet with only the occasional car. There are street lights but relatively few near the corner of King and Montague. The Wifi is good . Good for 1 night.

quebec-wild.name: Woodstock - Riverside
quebec-wild.notes:
Large gravel parking lot by the river. Quiet place with the added bonus of a superb sunset. Too bad there is a bit of waste. No sign prohibiting staying the night. We stayed 24 hours with no problems. Don't forget to leave the place clean with no trace of your passage, some people left trash on the ground and there is trash everywhere.  
.....
Grand stationnement de gravier au bord de la rivière. Endroit tranquille avec en prime, un superbe coucher de soleil. Dommage qu'il y ait un peu de déchets. Aucune pancarte interdisant de passer la nuit. Nous sommes restés 24 heures sans aucun problème.

quebec-wild.name: boat launch
quebec-wild.notes: A launch I stopped at for the night to get some rest. park off to the side to allow use of the boat launch. Not a long term spot, but definitely a nice quiet one!

quebec-wild.name: Le Bic by the River
quebec-wild.notes: Small site just next to the river le Bic and close to the 132.

Place for tent on car.

quebec-wild.name: the pylône spot

place under electric pylon, peace... view of the mountains, need a 4 x, 4

endroit sous pylône électrique, la paix... vue sur les montagnes, besoin d'un 4 x, 4

tranquille, chalets privés à proximité mais aucune personne nulle part... on s'est stationné dans le haut d'une côte !  belle vue et paix ! observation d'orignal en prime

little spot where we park for the trails and stayed overnight.
garbage and recycling bin
access to a few trails.
dry toilet across the road.

quebec-wild.name: Sia clairière madelaine centre
quebec-wild.notes: Super terrain plat pour camper, un peu en retrait du village. Il y a une petite épicerie et des toilettes dans Madeleine centre.

quebec-wild.name: Gooseberry Cove
quebec-wild.notes:
Beach/cliff side primitive camping. 

Turn off the paved road and follow signs for “Gooseberry Cove Trail”. Access road is narrow and rough. Accessible by SUVs and vans, anything larger is not advised. 

Cellular coverage is available but weak.

quebec-wild.name: fitzroy

quebec-wild.name: by the rapids

quebec-wild.name: K&P hut

quebec-wild.name: Belanger Lake

Beautiful spot during the weekday when it is quiet.
There is one easy spot for a camper van near the road and water, 
There are 2 more spots great for 4x4 overland rig near the pin (past a big mud hole ).

Keep it cleaner than when you arrived

quebec-wild.name: St-Jude, Province de Québec, près de St-Hyacinthe
quebec-wild.notes:
Very large parking. 
With very nice little park for children.
In front of a CLSC (mini hospital) close on weekend).
Perfectly quiet.

quebec-wild.name: Petite place boisée
quebec-wild.notes:
From the 132 and you take a small road (not well maintened but ok in a Grand Caravan) for about 300 m and you turn left to this site. 

If you continued on the main road, you will see private property, but stay behind that sign and fence. 

You can hear the highway (it’s not that bad) but you cannot see it. We weren’t disturbed by anyone. 

*They were no trash so keep it that way*

quebec-wild.name: Teapot Lake Pull Through
quebec-wild.notes: Big spot that can fit large trailers. There are two fire pits, a big one and a small one. Right on the lake and there is also an outhouse. The site is a little muddy because people usually ride ATVs around here.

quebec-wild.name: Sanddam Road
quebec-wild.notes:
Crown land. Been here for 3 nights and no one’s bothered me. I’m close to the road that leads to the dump (it’s far enough away so you don’t smell it.). Weekdays you do hear the dump trucks going by but it’s quiet by about 4 pm. There are several spots to camp, some nicer then this but I get 1-2 bars of cell here and none further up the road. 
A few ATV trails lead off this area but it’s been quiet, just the occasional one.

quebec-wild.name: Lakevale
quebec-wild.notes:
Fairly large parking lot
Definitely private land
But no barrier or prohibited parking
Near the river

quebec-wild.name: Acceuil Parson’s Pond
quebec-wild.notes:
Road stop at the entrance of the village. On the side of the road in an area 50km away, which is not very noisy. Picnic table and garbage can.
-----------------------
Alte routière a l’entrée du village. Sur le bord de la route dans une zone a 50km dont pas très bruyant. Table à picnic et poubelle.

quebec-wild.name: La martre

In front of the sea, a little after the village. Near the road, small path of about 200m leading to a plateau. In gravel

En face de la mer, un peu après le village.  Près de la route, petit sentier d’environ 200m  menant à un plateau. En gravier

quebec-wild.name: Saint-Maxime du mont louis

quebec-wild.name: Near the river
quebec-wild.notes: little spot near the river with fire ring. Lots of hiking trails. place for one rig. regular car can go there.

quebec-wild.name: Halte des Iroquois
quebec-wild.notes: This rest stop has several picnic tables, two very clean portapotties, garbage and recycling bins. There’s a view of the water on one side and highway 201 on the other. ( it’s only 2 lanes and not very busy at all )There’s some noise from the road but we expect that to calm down as night falls. We have looked around and do not see any signs saying we can’t camp here overnight. It’s a lovely little spot for a night

quebec-wild.name: TCT / Celtic Shores Coastal Trail
quebec-wild.notes: Beautiful spot by the ocean. This is a parking lot where the trail crosses Baxter's Cove Road. There are no "no camping" signs. Has cell reception.

quebec-wild.name: East of Woodstock
quebec-wild.notes: On highway 165, east of Woodstock NB is a paced huge lot between two bodies of water. Looks to be an old motel site. Beautiful spot, level and minimal highway noise

quebec-wild.name: Restaurant Miche-Main parking
quebec-wild.notes: Near to the road but many trucks are accepted for the nights... RV also accepted. It is a little truck stop restaurant/motel.

quebec-wild.name: Towards Cow Head
quebec-wild.notes:
St. Pauls , Highway 430 south side going towards Cow Head

No signs, gray billboard, trash cans, picnic tables

quebec-wild.name: Public land end of the road
quebec-wild.notes:
This place is at the end of the road, if you stop earlier you are not in the Public Land territory (you can see the limits on Google maps). 

The road is not the best, but we did it in a Grand Caravan with no problem. 

The site is pretty much a large clear area with rocks. Depends were you park it’s pretty flat. 

They’re a lot of room for different cars, even not on the same party. 

They’re bugs and mosquitoes and only a bar of cell service. 

This site is not the greatest, but if you want a lot of room and to see no people, this is the site.

quebec-wild.name: No Exit Street /near Hwy 11
quebec-wild.notes: Nice spot off the highway 11. It’s at the end of a no exit street. Entry point doable with a 4 x 4 or higher vehicle. No trailer. Open flat area with ample space. Perfect for one nighters during commute.

quebec-wild.name: grouse lake
quebec-wild.notes: beautiful high ground for 2 or 3 class b or smaller plus room for tents. we got our aluminum boat in by elbow grease but no problems for canoes or kayaks as there is a path/ramp. several great spots all along this road. road in is long 30-40 mins but not bad. no fish biting or jumping. atv's come through once in awhile

quebec-wild.name: sainte Agathe nord
quebec-wild.notes: on the Side of p'tit train du nord cycle path small beach ans small like on a private land not occupied ni mention of prohibited you have to go on left of the Fence. Bring bug repelent as close to water. fireplace in the Sand. good overnight place

quebec-wild.name: Open Hearth park
quebec-wild.notes: 2 paved parking lots and one Gravel lot. An employee of NS lands came by to chat and said it was fine to overnight here. No "no overnight" signs anywhere.

quebec-wild.name: Murray Head
quebec-wild.notes:
This is right at the end of the road. Enough place for 1-2 vans but probably nothing bigger. 

Quiet but plenty of mosquitos.  Lots of fishing boats roaming around.  Good 4G service on Rogers. 

According to the  Public Land Atlas this place is part of a Provincial Forest. 
http://www.gov.pe.ca/photos/original/gis_pubatlas32.pdf

Please clean after yourself and keep this place cleaner than you found it. Let's preserve such beautiful places. 

Stones now present for a firepit and appears to have been used.

quebec-wild.name: Baie de Tadoussac
quebec-wild.notes: Overnight parking permitted on the lower part of the parking lot. Accessible SEPAC toilets. Non-drinkable water. Nice view and right next to the ferry. --- Stationnement pour la nuit permis sur la partie de bas du stationnement. Toilettes de la SEPAC accessibles. Eau non potable. Belle vue et juste à côté du traversier.

quebec-wild.name: Riverside
quebec-wild.notes: 2 open sites next to each other.  Second site can be reached by an SUV through a really short but also tight trail.

quebec-wild.name: Lac Pomponne
quebec-wild.notes: Near a boat ramp.  Big flat area with some trees.  Very good place for a group.

quebec-wild.name: Boat ramp
quebec-wild.notes:
The boat ramp was closed at that time for the fisherman.  There's a 5 degree decline, so be prepared to level your vehicle.  It is also at 15 min from the road with a random passage of trucks.    After 2000 hrs, no one passes on the road.
You are 12 km from the village with gas.

quebec-wild.name: Apple River Road by water
quebec-wild.notes: Just after the bridge place for 2 small Rv's,road is a bit ruff to get there but was OK with my 24 foot class C. If you go further to spider's cove after the bridge ,the road will get a bit rough.went to Three Sisters hiking trail. there is a sign for camping if you go strait but we turned around when we could after going down hill and the road got to ruff for the Rv and went back to this site by the water enjoying the tide and a small fire. had some locals pass by and chat very friendly and road is very quiet even if it's by the road

quebec-wild.name: Service Road
quebec-wild.notes: Just as you are leaving Port Aux Basques past Grand Bay Road there is a turn off to the Service Road. Trucks park before/after ferry for rest. Two paved, mostly flat spots. Best for Vans, Trailers & RV's. No signs other than don't litter. Beautiful views. Great spot for the night before or after the ferry. LTE data here, strong cell signal.

quebec-wild.name: Pointe au bouleau
quebec-wild.notes: Excellent place to spend the night, for the more adventurous, you can go down just below with your camper to get closer to the water. there is no indication that camping is prohibited.

quebec-wild.name: magaguadavic river
quebec-wild.notes:
nice place on the side of the river. some traffic noise, but  quiet at night.
had a dip in the shallow river, it was perfect for a very hot day

quebec-wild.name: road side
quebec-wild.notes: road side. No sign saying it's forbidden, just below electric line, but very quiet few traffic during the day probably none during the night. haven't sleep here but could be a nice spot. could be avoided during melting snow season.

quebec-wild.name: Rivière des Petites Bergeronnes
quebec-wild.notes: This is not the best wild camp that you will find, but for this region, where it is difficult to find camping in nature, it is not too bad. The place is beside a track near the Rivière des Petites Bergeronnes. Unfortunately you can't go further to the Lac des Sables because the track is private. There is only one place for a small RV (20ft).

quebec-wild.name: Margaree Harbour
quebec-wild.notes:
Large mostly flat lot at the Margaree Harbour. No signs indicating no overnight parking. Be smart and don't park blocking any of the docks/wharf. Clean up after yourself & be respectful of the fisher folks.
Data/cell are reasonable here.

quebec-wild.name: Murray Corner Warf
quebec-wild.notes: Quiet spot besides the wharf. Didn’t see any no overnight parking signs. Stayed the night with no issues. Very quiet. Beautiful sunset and sunrise.

quebec-wild.name: South Gros Morne
quebec-wild.notes: Go west on 431 off 430 and the dirt road will be off to the right. You will pass a small quarry on the right and drive for quite a bit up a dirt path of a road. The road can handle a 4WD vehicle with maybe a small trailer. The site is a fairly large opening in the road to a flat area surrounded by trees and a lot of birds. Did see some Bear scat and Moose poop about 200m down the hill. You are pretty much on top of the hill but no views down but very nice and away from everything.

quebec-wild.name: Parc Carillon
quebec-wild.notes:
Beautiful place in a Canada's Park along the riverside. Pit toilet, water and tables are available. Super quiet place and really windy.

Très bel endroit le long de la rive. Toilettes, eau et tables disponibles sur place.  
Très tranquille et venteux.

quebec-wild.name: Hydro Line - Tree Cut
quebec-wild.notes: Cleared area around hydro lines, access via open trail East of where lines cross Hwy #118.  Had a pack (pair) of wolves pass my tent approx 9pm mid June 2022

quebec-wild.name: Abandoned logging Truck
quebec-wild.notes: The giant fire pit was taken and the other one was to close to the road so we came here. No one seems to be bothered by us. There’s bullet shells and old tires lying around, so not the most picturesque place and lots of mozzies, but very close to the park. There’s space for any type of vehicle here. No amenities.

quebec-wild.name: Forest
quebec-wild.notes: Small glade next to the track. You will be surrounded by trees with the sound of a small river and birds. Very quiet, you will be alone!

quebec-wild.name: Chemin des Piles Dead end
quebec-wild.notes: Atv, Side by side or Enduro bike. Easy access. No road showed on Google but use Apple map and its there.

quebec-wild.name: Veteran's Memorial Dr Boat Launch
quebec-wild.notes: There's a small opening for parking from the road that locals use for boat launch. It fits only 3 cars, so you may need to wait for night tike in order to park here, during the day on a nice weather it can be a bit busy with people going in and out. However, there's more parking space along the road by the ocean side just couple meters down. Because the parking is so small, I don't think it's appropriate for big rig, and it will not be level either mine is 17ft long and it fits perfectly, a bit tricky to get it level, but it works, see picture. For longer and bigger vehicle, go a few meters down as I mentioned earlier (see pic). The view is absolutely stunning, and the sound of the waves is so therapeutic to sleep with. No facilities or anything near by.

quebec-wild.name: Île Verte
quebec-wild.notes: Just in front of Ile-Verte. Tiny wharf. 2 picnic tables and trash bin. No interdiction sign. Room for 4 - 5 small RV. Windy but nice point of view

quebec-wild.name: Minas Basin
quebec-wild.notes: Super camp site , super nice view and quiet .

quebec-wild.name: Gabarus Lighthouse Open Space
quebec-wild.notes: A big open space by the ocean before getting to the light house (see pics). It doesn't look like the parking lot but I assume it is the parking for the lighthouse because you can't park at the lighthouse even though you can drive up. There's no parking next to the lighthouse, it's a dead-end road and quite narrow, at the end there's space to turn around, but if you park there and another vehicle comes up, they won't be able to turn around. Plus, this spot is more beautiful than the spot next to the lighthouse which is surrounded by bushes. The lighthouse is beautiful and very nice landscape, definitely worth a visit. It's super nice, quiet, and dark here. There's no facilities around, only a trash bin. Reception is very weak here, and I'm using telus, but if you go farther south toward St Peter's on Fleur de lis trail, many places do not have reception at all, and some part is long gravel road. If you go that way, make sure to fill up the gas tank and your vehicle is in good shape since there's no service around and you can't even call emergency. It's therapeutic to not have reception occasionally though.

quebec-wild.name: Rue Wilson sans pont
quebec-wild.notes:
Rue Wilson ends in a cul-de-sac where there is no longer a bridge (rivière aux vases?). This place seems used since there is a remnant of fire and waste.

La rue Wilson se termine en cul-de-sac là où il n’y a plus de pont (rivière aux vases?). Cet endroit semble utilisé puisqu’il y a un restant de feu et des déchets.

quebec-wild.name: Memorial St-Jean-Vianney
quebec-wild.notes:
A parking lot with picnic tables and a memorial to the St-Jean-Vianney tragedy. Lots of comings and goings in the area. Mountain bike trails nearby. Bring mosquito repellent.

Un stationnement avec tables de pique-nique et un memorial à la tragédie de St-Jean-Vianney. Beaucoup de va-et-vient dans le secteur. Pistes de VTT à côté. Apportez du chasse-moustique.

quebec-wild.name: Rue Roland
quebec-wild.notes:
Dead end.
There is no sign of « no parking »
Street not very wide: no big RV camper.
Near the forest.

quebec-wild.name: Rue Roméo
quebec-wild.notes:
Deep forest extremely close to the city.
Only one house at the end of the street.
No heavy trucks except local delivery.

quebec-wild.name: Wabush recreational parc
quebec-wild.notes: Recreational parc near a lake of cristal water, good place for a night, local people absolutely nice.

quebec-wild.name: Groves Point Park
quebec-wild.notes:
*Overnight parking/camping is NOT permitted at this location.

*Not open for camping/tent. Parks Canada.

Very beautiful park by the Bras D'or lake. It's super quiet here at night, very peaceful falling asleep with the waves. It's not too busy in the morning but it picks up in the afternoon. There are pit toilets and change room. No sign for no overnight parking or camping. Gates didn't close at night.

quebec-wild.name: motel
quebec-wild.notes:
Translation:parking behind the motel about 12 places including 6 with 110v provided by the city all for free

parking derriere le motel environ 12 emplacement dont 6 avec le 110v fourni par la ville le tout gratuitement

quebec-wild.name: Parking in front of pond
quebec-wild.notes: Gravel parking spot that fits a couple of RVs in front of a pond/lake. Parking area is not untouched but the lake is nice. Quiet place, rare noises from the road in front.

quebec-wild.name: Rte du Nord wild camp
quebec-wild.notes: Near km marker 329 is a road going to off to the south. It crosses under the electrical towers and curves behind some trees where you come to a couple of small parking spots. Small vehicles only, no fire pits or other facilities. Nice open and quiet spot.

quebec-wild.name: ATV Trail Head
quebec-wild.notes:
Quiet spot at the end of the road (road goes from pave to gravel, but well maintained). Very quiet, trails to roam and walk the dog. I think there is access to the water near this spot (locals fish and swim) but we did not explore the water this time.
Stanley is a great little town to hang out at. They have pretty much everything you need. Stop by Linda’s for a club sandwich and ice cream, down the hill across the street is the general store with attached NBLC, behind the store is the pharmacy (the street is easy to miss!!) and if you really enjoyed the community, drive past the pharmacy to the end of the road and to the right you will find Norma’s Boutique, a quaint little second hand shop used to support community members in need of help. Really great community.
And of course they have a post office and around the corner a gas bar with mini hardware store. The library is inside the school, everyone is pretty friendly and there is lots of green space of water to explore. The stars are amazing at night in this peaceful place, but bring your bug repellant!

quebec-wild.name: Close to St Ann's Provincial Park
quebec-wild.notes:
There's an opening space that leads to a dead-end road only a few meters before St Ann's Provincial Park. It looks like local people use this road for a boat ramp which is farther down the dirt road, looks almost like a trail to me. There was another camper from Quebec when I was there. So, for sure the place can fit at least 2 vans, I think maybe 3 camper vans is max. It has a decent view of the water, not that pretty but ok. A bit noisy when there are vehicles passing by during the day but very quiet at night. There's a pit toilet at the provincial park which is 10mins walk or less. If you go all the way to the dead end of the dirt road, there's a fire pit, looks like you can put up a tent there, and it would be a lot more quiet. Lastly, Telus reception is spotty here and very weak data service.   
.....
Endroit très bien au bas de la pente dans la courbe.

quebec-wild.name: Port au Choix # 3
quebec-wild.notes: Another spot along the shore just off the road. Quiet at night. Class B and smaller only. Great cell signal.

quebec-wild.name: Cape Smokey Provincial Park
quebec-wild.notes: Very peaceful, dark, and quiet at night, not too busy during the day either. There are 4 pit toilets. There's a long 10km trail or a short trail with the beautiful view of the cape. No sign for no overnight or no camping. Nice place to walk the dog in the morning and the view is so beautiful. Strong Telus reception here too with LTE+ data.

quebec-wild.name: Cap Lumiere
quebec-wild.notes: At the end of road - be prepared for a big sand pit in the middle! Only suitable for small SUVs (Honda Element for reference) and you can safely back into a  small parking area at a beach. Hidden from all the houses by bush. I've seen a couple of tents pitched on the beach even! saw someone had figured out a road further down from here with their vehicle when I walked the beach - so could be other options in the area, but I didn't see a road on maps. have fun!

quebec-wild.name: Discovery Beach
quebec-wild.notes:
By the ocean…Beautiful beach.
Much solace and windy.

quebec-wild.name: Christmas Island Cove
quebec-wild.notes: open area on beach. Sand a grassy area perfect to fit a few vehicles, could even set up a tent. Lots of garbage here when we arrived but cleaned up the area. We had a nice fire on the beach, and lots of sea glass to be found. Very quiet overnight

quebec-wild.name: Trail

quebec-wild.name: lac wallace rest area
quebec-wild.notes: nice litle spot for cars or bike, i dont know if we can sleep for a night but it seems quiet and there are toilets and picnic tables

quebec-wild.name: parking next too railway
quebec-wild.notes: parking next the railway. no services but ok for a night rest

quebec-wild.name: Ceilidh coastal trail

Nice place at the end of the road (you have to cross the cycle path) on the edge of the sea. Very quiet. Superb sunset.

quebec-wild.name: Parc des Parulines
quebec-wild.notes:

quebec-wild.name: Howley along trans Canadian trail

quebec-wild.name: Notre-Dame de la Merçie

Endroit très tranquille pour la nuit dans un cul-de-sac pour roulotte sans services ,près d’un lac et randonnée.

quebec-wild.name: little hiding place near of a lost barn
quebec-wild.notes:
There is a little spot you can go on the 105 road. To be honest, ils a little bit creepy with the fogetten barn and all the things inside and the noise of the sheet metal on the top of the barn. But, if you get over the creepy view from a horror moovies, you found a great place to sleep with a whole variety of nature. there are little rasberries and ruhbarb groth there. No signe you cannot sleep overthere for the night. I would recommend sleeping in a tent too. 
Over all, we would say its great for only one night.

quebec-wild.name: Mountain view

quebec-wild.name: Rivière-Port-Daniel rue de l'Église

quebec-wild.name: Hwy 113 Roadside

quebec-wild.name: Trailhead parking lot

quebec-wild.name: Braeside Beach

quebec-wild.name: Thomas Cove Coastal Reserve
quebec-wild.notes: Parking lot for Headlands and Economy Trailheads. No "no parking" signs. Approximately 4 km off Rt 2. Trees surround the lot, but the bay is a short walk down the trail. Barely any internet. Few hikers during the day but quiet at night.

quebec-wild.name: Boat ramp
quebec-wild.notes: Small spot by the highway near boat launch

quebec-wild.name: St Luke’s Presbyterian church
quebec-wild.notes:
There is a wide grassy area behind this closed/abandoned church, that is hidden from the road. A neighbour confirmed no-one comes around there anymore.
So I pitched my tent for the night while on a bike trip.

quebec-wild.name: Parrsboro Town Center
quebec-wild.notes: After a futile search for a spot to overnight, saw an RV Parking sign near the town bandstand. Another camper was already here. Couldn't find anyone to ask for permission and couldn't find any regulations online. Quiet night. Nothing like stealth parking in plain sight.

quebec-wild.name: Churchill River Crossing
quebec-wild.notes: Official paved rest area at west side of the highway bridge crossing the Churchill River. Large gravel area adjacent is right on the river. Lots of room.

quebec-wild.name: Near lake
quebec-wild.notes: A few campsite near the lakes. A few sites not so good for parking but quite a few are, mostly occupied during the weekend with atver's, quite and most are clean with already established fire pits.

quebec-wild.name: Little spot in the middle of nowhere
quebec-wild.notes:
I found this spot by chance because the Little pit was occupied. no water but quiet. big enough for 1 small tent or a small or medium van. There is a flat space on the spot and a pit to make a fire. a lot of black flies but that's normal in the woods... Isn't that right? 
----
J'ai trouvé ce spot par hasard car the Little pit était occupé. pas d'eau mais tranquille. assez grand pour 1 petite tente ou un petit ou moyen van. Il y a un espace plat sur le spot et un pit pour faire un feu. beaucoup de mouches noires mais c'est normal dans le bois... N'est ce pas?

quebec-wild.name: Foret Est
quebec-wild.notes:
Bring your bikes, 5 km of road suitable for vehicles and 9 km of very well maintained trails.
ATV and motocross prohibited.
In autumn, hunting is prohibited there.
1 rowboat and 1 pedal boat available on each of the 2 lakes as well as a kayak on the small round lake.
* for hikes on the lakes we ask you to wear a life jacket (compulsory) as well as a maximum of one hour per hike,
*Prohibited animals, we have our own (White-tailed deer, moose, otter, muskrat, raccoon, squirrels, flying squirrel, fox, porcupine, groundhog and beaver)
Magnificent little river in the middle of a cedar grove.
Little paradise for bird watchers (Wood duck, Mallard, Double-crested cormorant, Ring-necked duck, Crested merganser, Swamp sparrow, American Bittern, Red-winged blackbird, Great blue heron, Kingfisher, Common loon, Pileated woodpecker, Sparrow white-throated, Thrush sp., Waxwing, Ovenbird, Yellowthroat, Winter Wren ) and so on.
Lovers of forest and aquatic botany will be served as well as lovers of herbal medicine.
What about astronomy, no light pollution, I assure you that the Milky Way illuminates you in the middle of the night! The northern lights, more frequent in the forest because of the lack of light pollution, are breathtaking. Two shows in themselves for night owls who still have the energy to get to the dark.

quebec-wild.name: Large Quarry Site
quebec-wild.notes: Just west of km 375 on the north side of Rte 500. There are many such sites along the highway, but this one is really large, with parking spots ranging from on a lake to up on a hill. Many spots to park out of view from the highway.

quebec-wild.name: Église St Pierre de Becquets
quebec-wild.notes: Place for 4 RV authorized. For one night only. Some restrictions listed on the stair railing. Space furnished with picnic table. Very quiet with a magnificent view of the river.

quebec-wild.name: Le vignoble de la vallée des nuages
quebec-wild.notes:
Translation :Very friendly and welcoming people. With the purchase of products from the vineyard (excellent red and fortified wine!), you can sleep there for free. Terero member. Large parking space next to the vineyards. You must be independent.

Gens très sympathiques et accueillants. À l'achat de produits du vignoble (vin rouge et fortifié excellents!), vous pouvez y dormir gratuitement.  Membre Terero. Grand espace de stationnement à côté des vignes.  Vous devez être autonomes.

quebec-wild.name: Little Falls
quebec-wild.notes: On the Humber River west side before crossing bridge if coming from Deer Lake direction, about a dozen trailers with permanent fixtures. Person we talked with from one trailer said it is crown land. The photo is just off the gravel highway 422 before going down the hill where the trailers are located. We did not go to the end so maybe more spots. FYI - Route 422 from the other direction is a snowmobile track for about 4km and the rest is very rough although Google maps will send you that way.

quebec-wild.name: Parking near Lighthouse
quebec-wild.notes:
Next to a dam and an old lighthouse.

Stayed just to the side of the road as there was already an RV. We only stayed for the night and left early in the morning, but there was enough space for our small Element to camp without obstructing traffic

quebec-wild.name: Springbrook

Français

quebec-wild.name: Commercial Street

quebec-wild.name: Schooner Pond Cove

quebec-wild.name: Murray's Beach

Amazing local beach. 30 min. from
Port Aux Basques. Hard to find but let me tell you - SO WORTH it. The beach was empty around 6pm except for a few locals passing by ATV. Amazing view of the mountains and the swimming was perfect. The trail down is a bit rough but we have a cube van and made it ok. Just be careful on the beach. Honour and respect this place it’s a gem! Quiet night sleep and great chats with the locals if you're in the mood for that but everyone leaves you alone. Enjoy!

Spot right on the river. Used during the day by the people living near here to swim. Lots of ATV during the day and very calm and quiet during the night. Spent a night here without problem. There is no bathroom or showers but the river makes up for it. There is a little gravel road to get there easily done with any car or van. 
Lot of mosquitos when night fell. 
LTE and 5G work well .

quebec-wild.name: At junction near the river

Vast space on gravel, level.  Room for about twenty RVs.  No size limit.  5 minutes from Manic 5. No services on site.  Very quiet at night, very little traffic on the 138.

quebec-wild.name: Little Narrows ferry

quebec-wild.name: Table Point

quebec-wild.name: Club de ski de fond

quebec-wild.name: Morne de Saint-Sebastien parking lot

quebec-wild.name: Atholville Tide Head, Boom Road

quebec-wild.name: Blanc-Sablon

quebec-wild.name: Green Lake Campsite

quebec-wild.name: Dobson trail parking lot

quebec-wild.name: Lakeside
quebec-wild.notes:
Good spot for vans, pickups, etc. Not suitable for buses or big rigs.

Nice gravel area beside lake. Clean, Quiet(ish), no services. Full cell reception. You're 5m from a train line too but we haven't seen or heard a train in 7 hours... But your luck may differ Hehe. Not a long term spot but a solid overnighter.

quebec-wild.name: Riverside
quebec-wild.notes: A wide spot next to a river crossing on this dirt road. not the most level site, but it is workable. some soft sandy spots, beware. nice, fishy river. old fire ring and wood here as well. a little bit of car noise from the main highway but quiet at night. no Verizon service whatsoever.

quebec-wild.name: Longue Rive
quebec-wild.notes: We first went to the interpretation center (wifi and electricity) in Sault au Mouton, when leaving we turned right, crossed the river and after a few hundred meters  go right again ( after a small snackpoint) a small road and drive down to the sea. A beautifull spot, where the river come into the St. Lawrence bay. A gorgeous nice view over the bay with all the stones. No seals  or whales here. There are a few picnic tables and garbage bins. With room for tents and two vans.  There are a lot of rocks ( bumpy) but you can find a flat place at the other side of the Sault au Mouton river, at the back of the interpretation center. There is a short walk, a waterfall and a hanging bridge over the river.

quebec-wild.name: Sand quarry

quebec-wild.name: Tote road point

quebec-wild.name: Tail of Pinus River
quebec-wild.notes: At the end of a dirt road off the south side of route 500. Follow the road to the end. There are some stone painted marking the way. Large section for bigger rigs and groups. Smaller section near the river. We hauled a 27’ travel trailer in without issue. There is a ditch in the large section which can’t be passed with a trailer in tow but any vehicle can pass.

quebec-wild.name: Nice spot near ferry
quebec-wild.notes: Atv trail with a couple of big spots to park some rigs. Lots of blueberries.

quebec-wild.name: Labelle
quebec-wild.notes: A flat, big space near the 117. City approved for 2 nights.

quebec-wild.name: Street Parking
quebec-wild.notes: Parked overnight near the big park on the street. Spots are metered during the day, but not at night. No signs prohibiting overnight parking. Some traffic noise and light pollution. Cell data available. Okay for a night. No facilities super close, but after a short hike up a hill you'll be at the park itself and able to use those facilities.

quebec-wild.name: Trail head for chutes des denholm

quebec-wild.name: Deep pullout 20 km N. of Manic 5

The section from Gagnon to labrador border ("mine service road" near railroad with 10 to 15 railroad crossings is the section of the 389 that does not look like ready for prime time the next few years.
photo of deep pull out site. A few trucks around 10 pm and 7 am. Quiet in between. Certainly no locals!

quebec-wild.name: Clark city - rue de l’église

Stationnement éclairé au bout de la rue de l’église délimité par des grosse roche directement sur le bord de la plage de sable. Peux accueillir quelques véhicules campeurs. Une toilette « style chantier » est disponible sur place.

quebec-wild.name: Home Depot

quebec-wild.name: Dennis Beach

quebec-wild.name: Rte Allain turnoff

quebec-wild.name: Cape John
quebec-wild.notes: Curbside where there is room for 1 RV or tent, view on the ocean, little beach. No service and no garbage. Very nice spot but very windy. Locals were very friendly. Cute café nearby: the Overstreet café! :)

quebec-wild.name: Hill parking Kékéko

There are no "no overnight parking" signs and there is a chemical toilet in the summer time. The road is quiet at night. You just drive on the Témiscamingue Boulevard (leaving the town) and there will be a sign announcing Les Collines Kékeko

quebec-wild.name: off road pull in

quebec-wild.name: Cove side tree spot

quebec-wild.name: long mallory lake

quebec-wild.name: Rest area of ​​the Township of Lochaber Municipality

quebec-wild.name: Farm Point Chelsea

quebec-wild.name: Gravel pullout

quebec-wild.name: Mont Tremblant

quebec-wild.name: Roadside Paved Area

quebec-wild.name: Parc des  Chutes

Un bel endroit tranquille près d'un barrage, chutes et sentiers de randonnée, aucune interdiction de nuit. Nous avons passé une nuit tranquille sans problème.

quebec-wild.name: Queenstown picnic area

quebec-wild.name: Baie des roches

quebec-wild.name: Halte des Petits Lots

quebec-wild.name: Street parking near park

quebec-wild.name: Terrasse-Turcotte
quebec-wild.notes: Pay parking day time 9:00 to 18:00 1$ an hour but ticket guy said I can sleep overnight

quebec-wild.name: Mont-Tremblant Village Parking Lot
quebec-wild.notes:
New parking lot in Mont-Tremblant Village. No signs stating 'No Overnight Parking'. We had a great experience, it is right next to the beach as well. Washrooms during the day. Wifi! We were able to cook right outside our vehicle and had no problems. Plenty of restaurants nearby. 
Only some noise of trucks passing but nothing too loud.

quebec-wild.name: on the wharf in town
quebec-wild.notes: only parking we found is on the wharf good for 3 rv not more. No service.. Campground near by,was close for the season.

quebec-wild.name: Lac de la Rouche

quebec-wild.name: Patterson Wharf Park
quebec-wild.notes:
The community park at the end of King Street which if a narrow un paved dirt Road leading down to the water.  it has picnic tables a deck overlooking the water also has a barbeque and fireplace built of stone. No signage, can park on the road.  No washrooms, water, or Wi-Fi, but a beautiful stop. I don’t see why you couldn’t set up a tent. 
Restaurants up the road as well as other shops.  I parked under the bridge in front of a gate which serves to keep cars out, but there is an open access for pedestrians. The Bridge across the top, serves as a well maintained walking, hiking & biking trail also part of the trans Canada trail.

quebec-wild.name: Forest
quebec-wild.notes: Nice place to stay overnight. Totally lonely. The track up to the hill needs a bit higher clearance but not necessarily 4x4. It is stony and rough. For overlanders who like nature and silence. It is the beginning of a hunting area. In the beginning of a side track, you can find a good levelled places. We chose a spot which was obviously not in use for a long time. A few meters away down the side track you have a fantastic view over a lake.

quebec-wild.name: Roadside
quebec-wild.notes: Relatively large clearing with ample places to park.  Suitable for any sized vehicle, and tents as well.  There is access to water on one end, and more trails.  Several fire pits already. People come to not only camp, but launch canoes, dirt bike, ATV, etc. The bugs weren't too bad on the September long weekend, but in the spring, they can be awful. The road was fairly good, however it can be full of potholes, and washboards in spots, depending on what the weather has been- but still manageable with a car and some patience. No service with Koodo.

quebec-wild.name: Kegaska

Nous avons couché sur le quai, nous étions 2 RV.  Une personne qui pêche saisonnier nous a dit que nous n'aurions pas de problème à coucher ici, nous ne serions pas déranger.  Magnifique point de vue.

quebec-wild.name: Musée Louis-Langlois

quebec-wild.name: Opeongo River Site II

quebec-wild.name: Hidden parking lot next to trail

The most common one is the one crossing the train tracks. A lot of people come here during the day so you’ll see. No one bothers. This is a calm area.

quebec-wild.name: Close to Ferry

quebec-wild.name: McGowans corner, NB

quebec-wild.notes: a level parking area right in the middle of the village with a number of picnic tables and even a porta potty. I parked here overnight in my VW Westy with no problem. quebec-wild.name: No Name Lake

Great site on a lake with no name, beside Cedar Lake. Go down through Lower Madawaska Provincial Park, following Hyland Creek Road until it forks into Hyland Creek Road and Two Island Lake Road, staying left on Hyland Creek road you’ll come up on a dirt road on the right side. Follow it until the end and there’s a site on the left on Cedar Lake and one on the right on No Name Lake. 

Someone was on the Cedar Lake site but it looked massive (they had 3 trucks plus ATVs etc.) and that’s where the sunset pictured is. 
We stayed on the No Name Lake site and it was smaller and didn’t have the epic views but a great site none the less. All other Lake photos are no name lake- great for swimming and would be amazing if you had a canoe or kayak!

Great area for 4x4 driving around lots of dirt road, missing etc.

quebec-wild.name: Snowmobile Trail

quebec-wild.name: Rivière saumon by the water
