There are 6 or 7 individual spots for vehicles to park! Each has a picnic table and it’s own little bay to hang out in. 
The spots on either end of this causeway could accommodate larger RVs but the ones in between are smaller and best for vans or tents.

quebec-wild.name: Wildlife Management Area on Landing Rd
quebec-wild.notes:
There’s a small parking area at the end of Landing road  with room for about 3 cars. Longer rigs could park beside the trees. 
The road is quite potholed but if you go slow it’s manageable. 
We didn’t spend any time at the river as it started to rain as soon as we arrived. We wanted an alternative to the Canadian Tire or Walmart parking lot and this fit the bill perfectly. It’s quiet and private and there’s lots of trees around. No “no overnight camping” signs. 
There is a garbage can but no other facilities. There’s a hiking trail near the gate at the end of the road as well. Not sure how long it is or where it goes.

quebec-wild.name: The Old Pictou Railway Station
quebec-wild.notes: We liked this spot because it has a tall shelter that we could pull our van under to protect us from the rain while we cooked dinner on the bbq. It’s at the end of east Caladh Street overlooking the water. We checked out the laundromat as mentioned in another post. It’s the nicest one we have seen! Super clean with a bathroom and the option to just leave your laundry for them to do for you. Opens 8 am - 7 pm sharp.

quebec-wild.name: McAdam train station
quebec-wild.notes: Right next to train station so there is noise but only twice during the night so was ok. Road in front gets really quite after 6 pm 。gravel lot big enough to park 40foot rig with tow. No service. Telus has 4 bars so connection was good .

quebec-wild.name: Wagmatcook
quebec-wild.notes: Nice spot by the water. Close to the road, so could be a bit noisy at night. Did not find any signage saying No Overnight.

quebec-wild.name: By the dam
quebec-wild.notes: Cute little spot by the water. Has a established fire pit. Just off the road. Good for a night

quebec-wild.name: Rivière petit Calumet
quebec-wild.notes:
Access to the east side of the Petit Calumet river (sea side).
Two places to park. Further on, there are permanent residents. I don't know if it's really allowed, but the place is beautiful. Seen on the sea, the Egg Island and its lighthouse in front.
Without amenities, wild camping. We hear the cars passing on the 138, but it's not disturbing.
——
Accès côté est du ponceau de la rivière du Petit Calumet (côté mer).
Deux endroits pour se stationner. Plus loin, il y a des résidents permanents. Je ne sais pas si c'est réellement autorisé, mais l'endroit est magnifique. Vu sur la mer, l'Île aux oeufs et son phare devant.
Sans commodités, camping sauvage. Nous entendons les autos qui passent sur la 138, mais ce n'est pas dérangeant.

quebec-wild.name: The Brakewater the Val Comeau
quebec-wild.notes:
Peaceful place. For small Vr. You have to go around the provincial park and go to the end of the sand road. No prohibition. Access to the beach. Weak LTE network.
---
Endroit paisible. Pour petit Vr . On doit contourner le parc provincial et se rendre au bout de la route de sable . Aucune interdiction . Accès à la plage . Réseau LTE faible.

quebec-wild.name: Parc régional val D’Irène
quebec-wild.notes:
Large quiet parking with cellular network available. We asked for the Permission to of main cottage and
We are allowed to do it. In the parking lot only. Ideal site for a mountain hike!
——
Grand stationnement tranquille avec du réseau cellulaire de disponible . Nous avons demander la
Permission au chalet principal et
On nous la autoriser . Dans le stationnement seulement. Site idéal pour une rando en montagne !

quebec-wild.name: Chute Chalbert
quebec-wild.notes: Hiking Trail Parking near Chute Jalbert, 50 Meters to Hwy 132, not so windy as at the cost, at daytime noise but quiet at night

quebec-wild.name: Lighthouse Road
quebec-wild.notes: 28' motorhome will fit but no one else. beautiful place right on the shoreline. road to the lighthouse. made a campfire on the rocks at the ocean at night and watched the sunrise on the east coast of the Atlantic in the morning!

quebec-wild.name: Port Morien
quebec-wild.notes: Beautiful spot surrounded with beaches. Road network that spans the small peninsula. Multiple spots to camp. Road has some good puddles but a car would manage. 1 bar LTE with bell. Windy, amazing views. No services.

quebec-wild.name: True North Destinations
quebec-wild.notes: Opposite side of the little domes. we asked to stay and we asked for wifi. night was windy but very fine. would recommend. - beautiful overview of the ocean

quebec-wild.name: Lac La Paix
quebec-wild.notes:
Very nice place to camp for a weekend or a few days. Lots of spaces to isolate yourself if you want to be away.


Très bel endroit pour camper une fin de semaine ou quelques jours. Beaucoup d'espaces pour s'isoler si on désire être à l'écart.

quebec-wild.name: Small quiet place
quebec-wild.notes:
Small place front of NB power site and arena.
Stayed one night. There was a security guy all night and didn't say anything.
Perfect for one night during winter. 
During summer there is a big festival western of St Quentin.

quebec-wild.name: Tim Hortons truck stop
quebec-wild.notes:
Tim Hortons truck stop.
perfect for one night.
Many trucks came and go, not so quiet but safe.
Near to Tim Hortons so easy for bathroom.

quebec-wild.name: Hammock camp (No vehicle access)
quebec-wild.notes:
NO VEHICLE ACCESS
A camp I made at the lake and river meeting place perfect for a hammock with wood to gather for a fire. Just up from the bus camp.

quebec-wild.name: Mackenzie brook camp - No vehicle access
quebec-wild.notes:
No direct vehicle access, possible options nearby

Down the gravel road and across the bridge has quiet pullouts and creek camping in a tent. My camp is across the creek up in the trees as I have a hammock looking out to the tablelands.

quebec-wild.name: Thierry’s house
quebec-wild.notes:
Free overnight parking, wifi, couch/inflatable mattress, shower, etc. I’ve even got bikes you can borrow! 2 minutes walk from Main Street.

Paying it forward for other travellers! 

Contact me at Thierry.gaudreau@gmail.com

quebec-wild.name: Bilberry drive
quebec-wild.notes: Street parking overnight, close to park. Only need to worry about winter storm parking bans. Right next to park. Walking trails along Ottawa river close by. I have also camped in that area in a tent but it is a very popular area.

quebec-wild.name: Island
quebec-wild.notes: Island only accessible by boat. Secluded. Camped at this location in tents and hammock tents. Fire pit, beach, the area is in Quebec but most people speak English. It is technically private land but who knows who owns it. I’ve never heard of them being there

quebec-wild.name: Road side
quebec-wild.notes: Road side parking on a gravel lot behind A&W next to a farmers field. A couple of other vehicles here as we pulled in. Set back from the road. Quiet and safe.

quebec-wild.name: little lepreau basin
quebec-wild.notes: nice spot very quietly nice view many place 🌞

quebec-wild.name: Quack Head Lighthouse
quebec-wild.notes: Beautiful view overlooking bay of fundy and Nova Scotia in the distance.

quebec-wild.name: Street parking next to Lachine canal
quebec-wild.notes: Great location. Pretty quiet. There is a long strip of free parking directly next to the canal with lots of availability.

quebec-wild.name: Acordeon Museum
quebec-wild.notes:
Theres a small Carpark with some benches and trashbins. 
Not Big Rig friendly, just small RVs or vans.
Maybe be a little bit stealthy and dont be too loud you are in a neighbourhood. 

Over night Parking not allowed during winter(1. November till 15 April)
-Park is closed during 11pm till 5am.
-see pictures about the rules

quebec-wild.name: Stationnement Municipal Orford
quebec-wild.notes: Gravel parking near the Ruisseau David trailhead. No 'no overnight' parking sign. Very slow internet. No amenities. Spent the night here with no issue. Very quiet.

quebec-wild.name: Public boat ramp
quebec-wild.notes:
Small parking long to the water with a boat ramp, no sign of no overnight or parking.
--------

Beau petit stationnement près de l'eau et la descente a bateau public. petite parc avec table a pic nic

quebec-wild.name: Solar panel - Sorel
quebec-wild.notes: Au carré royal à Sorel tracy un bon spot

quebec-wild.name: Collines Béarn
quebec-wild.notes:
Large parking lot of the footpath of the Benarn hills. 2 km from the 109 road. Several places available. Fire place, chemical toilet, small space bbq, picnic table. Accessible for caravan, motorized. Tent OK. No prohibitions to sleep at night.
.....
Grand stationnement du sentier pédestre des collines béarn. À 2 km de la route 109. Plusieurs places disponibles. Fire place, toilette chimique, petit espace bbq, table de picnik. Accessible pour roulottes, motorisés. Tente ok mais plus ou moins confortable vu la gravelle. Pas de contre-indication pour dormir la nuit.

quebec-wild.name: Port de trois rivières
quebec-wild.notes: Lot of parking you pay 7$ for one night .. the night is 6h am until 6h am only the week end

quebec-wild.name: Forbes
quebec-wild.notes: Big gravel parking lot (for fishermen I guess) with grass on the sides. Entry direct from the main road, you can park up in the big place or drive down a small path for more privacy, a lot of space for tents too. No „no camping“ signs. Pit toilets and a picnic table, many fire places. A little hiking path to the river. We spend a quiet night.

quebec-wild.name: Chalk River close to town
quebec-wild.notes: Good spot to camp out, a bit of traffic, but seems like everyone is cool. Easy access right off a used dirt road off of hwy 17 west, an RV fits here for sure with space to turn around. A couple of trucks drove by, and they didn't seem to care. People from town also camp out here.

quebec-wild.name: Barrage merci baskatong
quebec-wild.notes:
Beautiful spots along the river 4x4 or suv recommended

Beau spots sur le bord de la rivière 4x4 ou suv recommandé

quebec-wild.name: Cap La Ronde, next to the beach
quebec-wild.notes: Beautiful spot, almost on the beach… place for one or two vehicles. Only accessible for little camper vans or 4x4 pickup truck campers. Lots of drift wood, so we made a campfire…

quebec-wild.name: Quartier Lairet
quebec-wild.notes:
free street parking at all times.
calm streets.
no amenities.

quebec-wild.name: residential boulevard
quebec-wild.notes:
free parking on the boulevard. 
exception : from 15:30 to 17:30, monday to friday

quebec-wild.name: Florence Beach
quebec-wild.notes: Small gravel parking lot on the road down to Florence beach. Follow ‘beach’ signs to the right on the road, parking lot is on the right about half way down. Don’t drive all the way down to the beach as there is no room to turn around. Quiet spot with beautiful sandy beach. No ‘no parking’ signs.

quebec-wild.name: Mont Rigaud - Sanctuaire Trail Head
quebec-wild.notes: Grassy/gravely parking area just below road up to the sanctuaire. No "no overnight parking" sign. Stayed here in a camper van. In cellphone range and close to the town of Rigaud (great town). Great place to stop if you want to rock climb or hike on Mount Rigaud.

quebec-wild.name: Chem. William Tremblay
quebec-wild.notes: Small parking area on a rock with à beautiful view of the Saint-Laurent River.  For small vehicles only.  No services.  Can fit 2 véhicules side by side.

quebec-wild.name: Halte RPA
quebec-wild.notes: Welcome to you nomads! If you’re passing by and are in need for a place to stay for the night, go ahead!

quebec-wild.name: Edmunston - Lions Park
quebec-wild.notes: Parking lot for the Lions Club Park. Good size parking lot next to residential area. Off of a relatively busy street but tucked in the back and quiet enough after 10 pm. Parking lot was large enough for bigger rigs to turn around.

quebec-wild.name: Gravel pit
quebec-wild.notes: Huge gravelled flat area, next to small lake not far from highway. there are several fire rings and minimal garbage.

quebec-wild.name: waiting for Fundy Trailway Park
quebec-wild.notes: waiting for the Trailway to open. coming from Fundy NP this is on the way. a dead end road with almost zero traffic in the whole area. just a plain dead end road..

quebec-wild.name: Old Pig Farm
quebec-wild.notes:
MODERATOR NOTE: destroyed pig farm - may be private property. Camping may not be allowed.

Super calm spot. !!4x4 Required with high ground clearance!! Could be muddy in some places and "might be" mosquito invested during summer.
There are different ways to get to this spot:
-Murray road near Rehau industries (short way mostly gravel)
-Melorse route (long, 1. asphalt 2. gravel 3. mud) but adventurous.

quebec-wild.name: Costangs Trail, Searston Entrance (North)
quebec-wild.notes:
Area for parking at the north end of the Costangs Trail. Road in is one lane, dirt road. Trail is less than 1km past a flat area that looks like a turn around (another spot good for the night). Will fit rigs of all size, if you don’t mind country driving. Space for 2/3 average size rigs.
Please do not block the “driveway” beside the building, the space around the building or entrance to the trail. No camping on the trail.
There is no wifi but there is good data signal. Sufficient for calls and internet use.
Trail closed 05.19.2023 because of storm damage. Usually fixed up by mid-June.

quebec-wild.name: Heppell covered bridge
quebec-wild.notes:
Nice quiet spot next to Heppel covered bridge built in 1909. River seems a local favourite for salmon fishing.
Two large areas easily accessible for RVs etc. No toilets but nicely secluded. No signs prohibiting camping.

quebec-wild.name: Guindon Park
quebec-wild.notes: Big daily park place with picnic table, garbages and toilets. Nice playground. No “no overnight” sign. Easy water acces

quebec-wild.name: Quebec tube clearing
quebec-wild.notes: Amazing spot, down a gravel road that is closed in the winter, cleared out lot with a large metal tube on it. Doesn’t look like anyone owns it. Peaceful and quiet.

quebec-wild.name: Gravel Lot
quebec-wild.notes:
Theres a Medium size gravel at the end of a Road where you can park for one night.
It's not that bright lighted during the night as the visitor center.

quebec-wild.name: parking near road
quebec-wild.notes:
Superb spot on a car park near the road, amenities nearby. Toilet, garbage can. View of the pond with hikes to do. Large playground for children. Tables for picnics, weekends should be avoided because music noises with sound system, otherwise quiet.
Ps: very good Italian restaurant not far away

Superbe spot sur un parking près de la route, commodités à côté. toilette, poubelle. Vue sur l'étang avec des marches à faire. Grand parc de jeux pour les enfants. Tables pour pique-niquer, les week-ends peut être à éviter car bruits musique avec sono, sinon tranquille. 
Ps: très bon restaurant italien pas très loin

quebec-wild.name: Aérodrome St-Jérôme
quebec-wild.notes:
Former airport which was used by a parachute school. Entrance from the rue de La montagne, dirt road. There is 1.5km of land on each side of the track. No signs prohibiting access (for the moment). We towed a trailer beyond.

Ancien aéroport qui était utilisé par une école de parachute. Entrée par la rue de La montagne, chemin de terre. Il y a 1.5km de terrain de chaque côté de la piste. Aucune signalisation qui interdit d’y accéder (pour le moment). Il y avait une roulotte delà.

quebec-wild.name: Boréal Régional Park parking
quebec-wild.notes:
Gravel parking with no "no parking sign". the park isn't maintained so it's kind of looking abandoned. some trails are nice and doable, some others aren't.
no toilets, no phone reception, but if you want to camp there before going for a hike, it's possible.

quebec-wild.name: Plumweseep covered bridge
quebec-wild.notes: Small site beside boat launch located just after you cross covered bridge.

quebec-wild.name: Muddy road, just before Jacques Cartier park
quebec-wild.notes: Just north of the Jacques Cartier Provincial Park on the right side of the road. It’s a pretty big parking lot with vehicle access to the beach.

quebec-wild.name: holt Mine Complex spot on the lake
quebec-wild.notes:
Translation: beautiful site directly on a small lake with the sunset in the background. Near the 101

beau site directement sur un petit lac avec le coucher de soleil en arrière plan. Près  de la 101

quebec-wild.name: West Point Lighthouse
quebec-wild.notes: Big parking lot that can accommodate big rigs. There is no 'no overnight parking' sign, so I'm assuming you can park overnight.

quebec-wild.name: Riverside
quebec-wild.notes: Super nice place for small rig, on the river with fire pit..... keep it clean ! it was not.

quebec-wild.name: Parking Montée de Wakeham
quebec-wild.notes: Big parking lot on Montée de Wakeham, right of Place Jacques-Cartier just behind the Paquepot Café. No sign saying that overnight parking is not allowed. Not a great view but calm at night until the morning traffic start around 7:30

quebec-wild.name: 24h parking pour pour VR / RV 24h parking spot
quebec-wild.notes:
Translation: Parking allowed for the night, there are several locations. Finally a place 100% authorized by the city!! at least 5 pitches, large spaces. no services. free.


stationnement permis pour la nuit, il y a plusieurs emplacements. Enfin un endroit 100% autorisé par la ville!!  au moins 5 emplacements, grands espaces. aucun service. gratuit.

quebec-wild.name: Glasford Lake
quebec-wild.notes:
Spacious area with boat launch. Room for about 6-8 Campers or tent sites. Great fishing in the Glasford Lake system. 
May need four-wheel drive or pickup to get to the camp site. Main road is in great condition but beaver dams have it underwater on occasion.

quebec-wild.name: Rabbit Lake
quebec-wild.notes: Spacious area. Room for approx. 10 Campers or tent sites. Open area looks to be an old logging camp at one time.  Located right next to Rabbit Lake Road with easy access.  Small pond across the road for water use.  Short half a km ride or walk to Rabbit Lake and boat launch area.

quebec-wild.name: Église Saint Michel De Bellechasse
quebec-wild.notes:
Nice place to sleep, no ban. park in one end, left early.
---
Belle endroit pour dormir ,pas d'interdiction.  stationner dans un bout, parti tôt.

quebec-wild.name: St-Elie-de-Caxton
quebec-wild.notes: Locals suggested the very back of the funeral home parking lot for overnight stay as they see many RVs there on a regular basis.

quebec-wild.name: Gooseberry Cove
quebec-wild.notes: Great spot for a peaceful night of sleep. Went there with a 4x4 and a roof tent, but could make it w/ a x2 or VR. Some parts of the site are hidden from the wind with the trees. Fire pit. Amazing view of Gooseberry Cove.

quebec-wild.name: Tatamagouche Public Parking
quebec-wild.notes: A large gravel car park one street behind Main St. Not level, but good enough for one night. Very quiet night, especially considering it was a Saturday night. Only sign states it’s public parking.

quebec-wild.name: centre récréatif St Marcel
quebec-wild.notes:
parking facing a schoolyard and park with a magnificent tennis court for amateurs. Absolute tranquility.
---
stationnement face à une cour d'école et parc avec un magnifique terrain de tennis pour les amateurs. D'une tranquillité absolue.

quebec-wild.name: Nestled in The Woods
quebec-wild.notes: simple drive in site surrounded by trees. no water. no "no camping signs.  large enough for 30 feet max.  off the highway .

quebec-wild.name: Halte Bond
quebec-wild.notes:
RV camping stopover overlooking the sea on Howard Bond's lot on the edge of the 132. Mr. Bond charges $20 and goes to the lot in the evening to collect.
--------
Halte camping pour VR avec vue sur la mer sur le terrain de Howard Bond au bord de la 132. Monsieur Bond charge 20$ et passe au terrain en soirée pour collecter.

quebec-wild.name: Pointe-Claire Village Public Parking
quebec-wild.notes:
Parking near the village. many spaces available. Good for Sprinters, not for bigger TVs.
.....
Coin très sympa proche de la ville, plusieurs place de parking disponible. C’est pour des véhicules types sprinter, pas de vr.

quebec-wild.name: Place
quebec-wild.notes:
Big parking place, quiet, no car on the driveway. No “No parking” sign.

I stay here for one night sleeping in my car. 
Many cars can be here and maybe tents can be stop here too. 

No disturb

quebec-wild.name: 1re Rue Parking lot
quebec-wild.notes: A small, informal muddy parking lot along a gravel road. Probably used by truckers to make a turn. No "overnight camping prohibited" signs. Good for a night. Space for 2 vans, I guess.

quebec-wild.name: Little river in the woods
quebec-wild.notes:
Nice spot near a small river/brook. Fire pit. Space for 2 to 3 small tents or 1 or 2 RVs. Parking space. Close to a road but not very busy.
---
Joli endroit près d'une petite rivière/ ruisseau. Pit à feu. Place pour 2 à 3 petites tentes ou 1 ou 2 VR. Place pour stationner. Près d'une route mais peu passante.

quebec-wild.name: Secteur l’Energie
quebec-wild.notes: 8 places for RV equipped by "Le parc régional des grandes rivières " 6km of passable track to get there. 8 places pour VR de toutes tailles. Sentiers de randonnée sur place.

quebec-wild.name: Nice rest
quebec-wild.notes: A nice spot near the road (you can hear some noise) no interdiction sign. a lot of room but not for big rv because of the dirt road before.

quebec-wild.name: Chemin des chutes
quebec-wild.notes:
Parking with 5 places, toilets, big park with a nice river. We stayed the night and enjoyed it. We were 4 people during the night (3VR and one pickup) and 1 more with a regular car in the morning. Lot of mosquitos. No camping sign for tents.

Parking avec 5 places, wc, cabine pour se changer, gazebos, belle rivière avec un pont typique de la région. Très pratique.
On était 4 pendant la nuit (3 vans + 1 pickup) et 5 au petit matin, avec une voiture en plus. Beaucoup de moustiques. Panneau « NO CAMPING » pour les tentes.

quebec-wild.name: Marble Drive Trailhead
quebec-wild.notes: Small gravel parking area, with rubbish bin. You can see the ski slopes through the trees, which also buffer the highway noise. No  signs prohibiting overnight parking. Will accommodate 2 <25' Campervans only.  Cell signal. Not far from Tim Hortons and Exit 8.

quebec-wild.name: Boat launch
quebec-wild.notes: Boat launch next to Shortts Lake. Beautiful lake. Road next to it is pretty quiet, especially at night. There’s a plant close to the site, but didn’t experience the noise as disturbing (when you’re outside it sounds like a motor engine idling in the distance).

quebec-wild.name: Notre-Dame-de-Lorette
quebec-wild.notes:
2 places for RV very quiet in the forest in « le parc régional des grandes rivières »
2 places pour RV max 7,5m mises à disposition par le parc.

quebec-wild.name: Standstead Church
quebec-wild.notes: Large parking at the church. No sign of no-camping or no parking overnight. We slept in the parking lot. Very quiet. Nobody disturb us or anything.

quebec-wild.name: Roy G Hobbs Community Centre Park
quebec-wild.notes: A very small parking lot next to the Ottawa River Pathway and an off leash dog park. A quiet place with minimal traffic in the evening. I didn’t investigate the ports potty. No posted signs.

quebec-wild.name: Baxters Corner Beach
quebec-wild.notes:
Roadside parking along the beach of the lake. Spent one night. Super quiet. No sign of any kind. 

It is a community, and there is a house at the end of the street. Please be mindful and don’t litter. 

Gorgeous spot.

quebec-wild.name: gravel pit
quebec-wild.notes: Gravel pit off westbound 510 in Labrador. Nothing special, but plenty of room without being right on the highway. Old trailer on site.

quebec-wild.name: Bicycle path parking along tomifobia  trail
quebec-wild.notes: Room for 2/3 vehicles, one picnic table and garbage can at ours disposal. Along route 141 really close, but quiet at night

quebec-wild.name: Below a power line
quebec-wild.notes: Nice spot under the power line. Just before the Pourvoirie.

quebec-wild.name: Wild Parking St-Laurent river
quebec-wild.notes: Beautiful spot with a long walking path next to the St-Laurent river with a view on some islands. Quiet place, no sign for no parking overnight. No amenities, but there's some chemical toilet next to the walking pathway. There are also some picnic tables! (if you're in the parking lot)

quebec-wild.name: Fundy parkway entrance
quebec-wild.notes: Dirt road. Nothing fancy but ok to sleep one night before getting in the Park.

quebec-wild.name: No Stormy
quebec-wild.notes: When very stormy by coast, you can here standing to overnight. It's near a little river in curved a road without overlook to the sea.

quebec-wild.name: Next to the water
quebec-wild.notes: Got lost and found this place. Didn’t stay the night but seems pretty great for overnight camping. A small gravel road leads you to a small field right next to the ocean. No private property sign

quebec-wild.name: The large spot
quebec-wild.notes: Found on Lac Vert. This island offers 3 or 4 good camping spots. This gps location is the buggest camping spot out of the four. There can easily be 6-7 tent. There is a little table, for cooking (made my hand) and a private beach.

quebec-wild.name: Vélo piste Jacques Cartier/Portneuf
quebec-wild.notes: Gravel parking for bike path. Next to a park. Quiet.

quebec-wild.name: Public Beach along river
quebec-wild.notes:
Stayed here a couple times, very busy until late at night.  Locals water hole as well, normally I swim but that water could be super gross if you're picky about that kinda stuff.  Access way to parking is very tight, narrow, full of big potholes and sandy, for sure nothing bigger than a medium size van here but 4x4 not required.  No toilets

Ich war ein paar Mal hier, sehr beschäftigt bis spät in die Nacht.  Einheimische Wasserloch als auch, normalerweise ich schwimmen, aber das Wasser könnte super ekelhaft sein, wenn Sie über diese Art von Zeug wählerisch sind.

quebec-wild.name: Pink beach
quebec-wild.notes:
Beautiful place to take a break or to spend the night, right beside the beach. Clean dry toilet and picnic tables. There is an interdiction to set up a tent and to make a fire, but nothing else. I spent the night without any problems. Great view on the stars. 
That's a place where locals go, but I still felt safe. Dogs needs to be on leash.

quebec-wild.name: Public Parking
quebec-wild.notes:
*No overnight camping allowed. 
Big asphalt parking lot in between baseball and soccer fields in a big park. Free parking. There are picnic tables, trash cans, a water fountain, and most likely toilets in the building when open but we haven't checked.

quebec-wild.name: Grass Cove Beach
quebec-wild.notes: Mostly level gravel pulloffs in a grassy area next to the beach. This area is visited by locals and is clean and quiet. This place was suggested to us by a local and a few other locals spent the night here as well. We were told it is public land.

quebec-wild.name: Free street parking
quebec-wild.notes:
Free street parking next to an office building. We stayed her two nights during the weekend and had no problems and felt safe. There are a lot of joggers and circlers. There is a train track next to the street, so it's something quite noisy. 
To mile end and little Italy, which both districts have a lot of bars and restaurants, it's both just around 20 min walk.
check the photo with the parking hours!

quebec-wild.name: Quai des Pêcheurs Cap-Egmont
quebec-wild.notes:
Large parking lot near the Cap-Egmont fishermen's wharf. Very quiet, beautiful view of the sea!
--
Grand stationnement près du quai des pêcheurs de Cap-Egmont. Très tranquille, belle vue sur la mer!

quebec-wild.name: Dirt road pull off
quebec-wild.notes: Need high clearance to get here. Just over the hill and there’s an extended circle in the road with a fire pit. Wide enough for a truck to be on one side to lower others pass. Not a soul came by over night. Established ring on site. Some kind of frogs were croaking at each other over night and into the morning.

quebec-wild.name: Gravel clearing
quebec-wild.notes: You’ll need high clearance for this spot. Large gravel area. Come in on the left to avoid some sand. Not sheltered but there are some level spots.

quebec-wild.name: Near beaver pond
quebec-wild.notes: You’ll need 4x4 and clearance to get here. Just after the beaver pond there’s a spot on the right. Somewhat level and off to the side of the dirt road. Very quiet and peaceful.

quebec-wild.name: Old bridge
quebec-wild.notes: Nice little hidden place next to a stream. Quiet and reasonably flat and protected from the wind

quebec-wild.name: Street parking at a park
quebec-wild.notes:
There is a small circle at the end of a street. It's directly in a park where you can hang out and it's just 20min walk to downtown.
Between 9 am and 4 pm it's just allowed to park for 2 hours. After that there is no regulation and we stayed here overnight which was no problem. It's not so good for big RV,s I guess

quebec-wild.name: Camping La Chute
quebec-wild.notes:
Tenting spots near Chutes Jalbert. 700m up the trail from the road. 2 pads for tents. A hit that you could sleep up to 4 people. Pit toilet, bring your own TP.  Firepit and picnic bench. Seems like a nice spot to camp. 

Seems free, couldn't find any info on site.

quebec-wild.name: Lost Street
quebec-wild.notes: Short dead-end street that seems to have never been used, and forgotten once the Dix30 shopping center was built nearby. fairly close to highway but not that loud as it is surrounded by trees. Very close to shopping mall and restaurants. Nothing crazy about this spot but a great place for a quick stop for the night.

quebec-wild.name: Abandoned Campground
quebec-wild.notes: Abandoned campsite with playground, mini-golf, abandoned tennis courts. We spent the night and had no issues. There are still picnic tables and firepits. A "Wild Camping" sign indicates the old pitches but the vegetation has regained its rights.

quebec-wild.name: Bar St entrance to Minister Island
quebec-wild.notes: This is a gravel lot that opens up to a road to Minister Island at low tide.  No toilet, no water but what a spot to watch the tides change.  We spent one night a few cars wandered down this way but no one bothered us.  There are no ‘no camping or overnight parking’ signs.  There is a garbage can.

quebec-wild.name: Park
quebec-wild.notes:
I found this river view spot via iOverlander last night, but when I went to check in this morning, it was not showing up on the list no matter how I changed the settings.

This is a small public parking area with room for about 10 cars to pull nose in. When I got here at midnight, there was one other car here. When I woke up at 5 am nearly all the spots are full of local cars. A few parked to go fishing on the pier and others were biking or jogging.

There is a road behind the parking spots that had a fairly steady stream of traffic throughout the night. It was otherwise quiet. I felt safe.

The best part was that I was able to walk along the river to a nearby Arboretum.

quebec-wild.name: Halte Maritime
quebec-wild.notes: Small park and parking lot before the bridge. Good place for a few hours stop. We stayed overnight 11pm-7am no one bothered us.  Very loud due to traffic.

quebec-wild.name: cliff with a view
quebec-wild.notes: A nice cliff with a great view on the bay of Fundy. The road is probably for 4x4.

quebec-wild.name: Street parking downtown - free weekends
quebec-wild.notes: Nice and quiet part of downtown Trois-Rivières, walking distance from restaurants and bars, Museum Pop, and not too far from the waterfront. Several coffee shops all within walking distance as well. It's meters during the week and free during the weekend. Some parts of the street are flat, some perfectly level.

quebec-wild.name: Shediac Trail Head Parking Lot
quebec-wild.notes: Outhouse and no “no parking” signs. Big enough lot to have 6 vans parked side by side in 2 rows. Relatively level with gravel so you shouldn’t sink in the rain.

quebec-wild.name: Parking lot at the Charlottetown farmers market
quebec-wild.notes: Parking lot next to the Charlottetown farmer’s market. Please respect that the parking lot is for customers of the market when it’s open on Saturdays. It’s a good place to stay and it’s close to the university Ave in Charlottetown but the traffic is pretty quiet over night. There are a few picnic tables as well. Please take everything you’re bringing with you to keep the place clean :)

quebec-wild.name: Constance Bay Beach - Street Parking
quebec-wild.notes: Street parking with beach access all along the several km beach.  Beach access is marked with blue sign with three white lines.  By-Law is that you can park overnight on the street and up to two hours between 7-7 on weekdays and 6 hrs on weekends. Gorgeous Sandy beach with miles of walking in either direction. This is a residential area and folks may not love vanlifers hanging around but so long as we follow the bylaws we have as much right to enjoy this 'one of a kind' beach as anyone.

quebec-wild.name: Ottawa River
quebec-wild.notes: River access spot at the end of Dunrobin Road:  There is a small flat area on sand, if you’re confident you can get off it. Otherwise good spot for a dip in the river on a hot day.

quebec-wild.name: Lac Limony
quebec-wild.notes:
Nice quiet spot with access to the lake.
Some locals during the evening to take a dip into the lake but alone all night. Place for 2 camps.
Very enjoyable! Keep it clean!

quebec-wild.name: Ottawa River Walk-In Camp
quebec-wild.notes: This specific plot of land is largely ignored by the city. It's by far the most scenic view of the Ottawa River from central Pembroke. Its sheltered and private from the main Millennium Trail behind the Beer Store. No anti-camping signage, and the homeless of town haven't had issues occupying the various tent-camping spots available. Within walking distance of many amenities in town. River is shallow for quite a distance, but is still considered swimable! Accessible stairs from Algonquin Trail down to waterfront or Beach just a few more steps down trail...

quebec-wild.name: Stationnement centre communautaire pointe au pere
quebec-wild.notes: Parking where you can stay 24h max. Be careful during snow removal operation between november 1st - april 15th (11pm-6am).

quebec-wild.name: MacLaggan Bridge
quebec-wild.notes: Overlooking the Nashwaak River. Three spots suitable for parking camper vans all in very close proximity to one another. Two sites are flat enough for tenting. Woods road follows the river upstream for an easy hike. Birds & waterfowl to observe.

quebec-wild.name: Whalecome & Octopus Ice Cream Gravel Lot
quebec-wild.notes:
Gravel lot for several small businesses and wharf area. No signs are posted that indicate “no parking”. Located on the west side of the new covered bridge.

The lot is very crowded during business hours, and we arrived @ 9 pm and spent one night here with one other camper and departed early. Easy parking for small rigs and camper vans. Take care during lobster season, there are several vessels moored at the wharf here and likely to be more fishing related traffic during lobster season.

AT&T cell service slow.

quebec-wild.name: Belvédère Havre-Saint-Pierre
quebec-wild.notes:
Belvédère 5 min après Havre-Saint-Pierre direction est. Nous etions 6 petits rv hier. Belle plage juste en bas.

Look out 5 min after Havre-Saint-Pierre east direction. We were 6 small rv. Nice beach just below.

quebec-wild.name: SOS box 272
quebec-wild.notes:
Nothing special, just a safe flat space to pull over on Trans Labrador highway. There is an sos phone box :)
Google says gas station is 45km ahead. Manic 5 60km behind. 
Zero cell service, but starlink works :)

quebec-wild.name: Staffing area

Large (couple acres) flat graded gravel area right beside the highway with easy access. 
Big rig friendly,  with room for dozens

From Percé the road to get there is paved but very step, maybe 20%.

quebec-wild.name: Along Labrador Highway

quebec-wild.name: Parking past Dunes Campground

At the end of the road when you're in Percy there is free parking :)

quebec-wild.name: Super C (G4X 2L2)

quebec-wild.name: Aylmer

Sur le côté du chemin de terre dans le tournant, une vue superbe sur la rivière des Outaouais. Fin juillet et août, un pommier vous offre ses fruits. Aucune facilité disponible si ce n'est que de grosses pierres qui peuvent servir de tables et de bancs.

CAUTION small sink-hole at the edge of the road on one side.   Small falls below the bridge. Trail to hike down below the falls through the woods.

quebec-wild.name: Lac Larose

Public Land accessible by trail. Be careful a lot of mountain bikes and motorcycles. It can also have party people but it's relatively quiet. The road is maintained by the city of St-Mathieu. Do not rely on Google map because it does not indicate any road. Follow road 724 towards Lac à la Coureuse then follow the indications towards Lac Larose.
---
Public Land accessible par la trail. Attention beaucoup de VTT et de moto. Il peut aussi avoir des fêtards mais c'est relativement calme. La route est entretenu par la ville de st-mathieu. Ne pas se fier à Google map car il n'indique aucune route. Suivre le chemin 724 vers lac à la coureuse puis suivre indications vers lac larose.

quebec-wild.name: Portage Lake
